segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: We are having a good conversation.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᏊ’Ꮫ ᏥᎦᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᎯᎾ ᏱᏗᏃᎲᎳ, ᏥᏗᏃᎮᎠ,
segments.translation: That is what I am saying. It’s good we can just talk about this.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꮽ Ꮎ ᎩᎶ ᏣᎩᏃᏎᎸ Ꮎ … ᎤᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᏗᏁᎯ, Carolinas ᎤᎾ,ᏚᎵᎲ Ꭱ…ᎢᎦᏖᎳ,ᏗᏍᏗ ᎤᎾ … ᏦᏍᎪᎯ’Ꮕ, … How do you say “acres?” ᏦᏍᎪᎯ, ᏱᎩᏓ, ᏱᎬᎾ,ᏕᎾ, ᎦᏙᎯ, ᎠᏓᎲᏍᎬ, ᎨᎮ … yeah, and build you a house. Ꭲ-ᎢᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᏱᏣᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ,
segments.translation: Someone was telling me that those who live that way in the Carolinas, they were wanting us to join them there. And 30 – how do you say acres? That big, 30, they would give you that size of land. Yeah, and build you a house if you go that way.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Are we going there?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: But then, you would have to--ᏃᏭ, Ꮭ’Ꭾ ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ ᏱᏣᎭ, Ꮎ ᎯᎢ ᏥᏂᎬᏁᎠ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏥᎩᏍᏕᎵᎠ, I guess, ᎤᏅᏌ, ᎮᎾ, ᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁᎠ, the Cherokee Band ᎤᎾ eastern Oklahoma, or … Carolinas.
segments.translation: But then you would not have a doctor. Like how they are doing here, how they help. I guess they are doing it themselves the Cherokee band there in eastern Oklahoma or Carolinas.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Have you heard that?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, EBC[I] Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᏍᏗ, … ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᎤᎾ,ᏕᏅ or ‘ᏙᎬ ᏴᏓ? ᎤᎾ ᎤᎾ,ᏕᏂᏙᎸ
segments.translation: Really, the EBCI is not like that. If they are born there, or what would you say, lived around there.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Where they grew up.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Yeah. Yeah. That’s the only ones that can have property on that reservation.
segments.translation: Yeah. Yeah. That’s the only ones that can have property on that reservation.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮕ ᏍᏊ ᏔᎵ’Ꮽ, … Okay, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᎩᎭ ᏏᏉᏯ ᏧᏬᏪᎳᏅ ᎤᏠᏱᏍᎪ, ᏄᏅᎿ,?
segments.translation: And secondly, OK, the Cherokee we have, that Sequoyah wrote, do they have the same thing?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, they still use the same thing.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: And our language is that much different?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Yeah, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏓᎬᏃᏎᎵ, ᏗᏗᏍᏆᏛᎢ … ᏯᏕᎳᎰᎯ, ᏄᏍᏗᏓᏕᎬ ᎤᎾ ᏗᏢ,
segments.translation: Yes, I am going to tell you something. When we are finished, you can find out how it is that way.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Okay.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᎯᎾ Ꮎ ᏣᏓ ᏥᏗᏃᎮᏍᎬ y’know ᎩᎳ,’Ꮽ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏍᎩᎾ … Ꭷ… Ꭷ ᎣᏣᎵᎮᎵᎦ, ᏤᏗ Billy
segments.translation: This is good, what we were talking about a little bit ago. That’s good. Now we are glad you came Billy.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Alright, I am, too.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: What is your name in English?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Billy Ray Pettit.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: What about in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Unihvlugi.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Unihvlugi, where did that come from?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: I guess my dad.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Is that who named you, your dad?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: What is that?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: “Waiting for ambush.”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh, really? Unihvlugi.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: That is why people are always chasing me around.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You have a good name.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ “Waiting for ambush.” … ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᏥᏂ,ᎬᎩᏪᎮᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ Wisconsin ᏴᏫ, ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, they didn’t know me by Billy. ᏍᎩ ᏥᎬᏬᎮᎲ “ᎤᏂᎲᎷᎩ,” … ᎤᏂᎪᏓ, and I knew a lot of people in Wisconsin.
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s it, waiting for ambush. That is what the people in Wisconsin used to call me, the white people. They didn’t know me by Billy. That is what they called me – Unihvlugi. A lot of them, I knew a lot of people in Wisconsin.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Is that right?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: And there were a lot of whites and a lot of blacks, too. ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏍᎩ ᏥᏂ,ᎬᎩᏪᎮᎲ “ᎤᏂᎲᎷᎩ,”
segments.translation: There are a lot of whites, a lot of blacks, too, but they all called me that, Unihvlugi.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: How long did you live there?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: 19 years, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Wow, what were you doing there?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏅᏃᎯ, ᏥᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ road construction. … Ꮭ’Ᏺ ᏗᎦᎨᏓ, equipment, ᏱᏗᏥᎯᎵᏙᎮ I was just a shovel and sledgehammer. That was my favorite, yep.
segments.translation: I was working on the road, doing road construction. I wasn’t driving heavy equipment, just a shovel and sledgehammer. That’s my favorite.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: So, you really worked hard?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: You betchaa! Now I am crippled.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You still do a little bit, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Oh, yeah, Ꮟ’Ꮫ remodel ᏱᏂ,ᏕᎬᎦ, ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ yeah
segments.translation: Oh yeah, I can still remodel houses, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: When were you born?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: … ᏣᎳᎩᏍᎪ, ᏍᏊ ᏯᎩ-ᏯᎩᏪᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾ? Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩᎾ,’Ᏺ
segments.translation: Do I have to say that in Cherokee? I don’t know that.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You can say it in English.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: When I was born was 1962.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: We are the same age.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, February 5th I was born. What about you?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: The 10th.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: February?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Well I say! Good people born in February.
segments.translation: Well I say! Good people born in February.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: And Mom was the third. That was her birthday.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Well son of a gun! Wow!
segments.translation: Well son of a gun! Wow!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: We are good people!

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: [laughter] Heck yeah!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Where was it you were born?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎠᎭᏂ,’Ꮫ ᏓᎵᏆ, yeah, ᎠᏭ’Ꭸ Ꮎ that … ᎭᏢ’Ᏼ? By the college?
segments.translation: Here in Tahlequah. Yeah, over there, where would you say? By the college?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I guess it’s that.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, by the college.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, yeah, ᎤᎾᎾ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏥᏩᎩᏴᏢ Ꮎ’Ꮫ Dickie ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᏃᏭ ᏁᎲᎾ, ᏥᏯᏘᏂᏙᎲ he was diabetic. ᏥᏯᏛᏛᏅ nurse, “Can I walk around?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Well, yeah!” ᏧᏛᏅ “This is part of your facility.” ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, ᏩᎩᏴᏢ ᏥᏙᎬ ᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ “’Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ, ᏕᏣᏙᎠ,?” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎩᎶ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎠᎨᏯ, ᏥᏃᏎᎸ “Mm! Mm! ᏂᎯ ᏍᎩᎾᎢ!” – “ᎠᏯ’Ꮫ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎤᎾ’Ꭱ ᏥᏫ,ᏘᎧᎾ,” ᏧᏛᏅ “ᎤᎾᎾ ᏥᏅ,Ꭼ ᏂᎯ,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ I was at that door, where I was born at. ᎤᎾ’Ꭱ ᏥᏫ,ᏥᏯᎥ … ᏥᏥᏙᎬ door-Ꭲ “ᎠᎭᏂ,’Ꭱ ᏂᎯ ᏥᏯᎥ ᏥᏣ,ᏍᏗᎬ” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ
segments.translation: By NSU, yeah. I went in there one time when Dickie passed away. When he died. I was taking him in – he was diabetic. I asked the nurse if I could walk around, and she said yes. This is part of your facility, so I went in there. I was standing in the door and some old lady said, “What is your name?” I told her, and she said, “Mmmmm…” She said, “You are him?” and I said, “I am him.” She said, “Where you were looking, you were laying there.” I was at that door where I was born. I was in there or standing at the door. She said, “You were in here when you were little,” she told me, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Is that right?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, it was just some old lady. ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ,
segments.translation: Yeah, it was some old lady that spoke in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Do you read Cherokee or write it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏍᏗ ᏱᏥᎪᎵᏯ, ᏚᏍᏆᎸᏛ ᏍᏗ … ᎤᎾ ᎠᏬᏪᎶᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ,’Ꭱ ᎠᏩᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏍᎩᎾ …. ᎾᎾ ᏥᎩ, ᎠᏂ-Jehovah Witnesses ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎧᎵ ᏯᏂᏬᎯ, ᏣᎳᎩ,
segments.translation: I can read a little bit, very little. Yeah, I would want to write to learn all of that. Like those Jehovah’s Witnesses, they can fluently speak Cherokee.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They were at Dad’s.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Jarred Hammer-Ꭲ’Ꭸ? Tyler Hodge-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, ᎠᎬᎿᎨ ᎠᏘᏁᎲ ᎠᎨᏯ,
segments.translation: Was it Jarred Hammer and Tyler Hodge, he had a black woman with him?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes, and a Japanese girl.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That girl was talking Cherokee.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, you betcha. Ꮵ-ᏥᏬᎨᏙᎸ Ꮎ ᏧᏂ,-ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ Westville to go visit them. ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏧᎾᎵ,ᏣᏙᏅ ᏁᎳᎩ’Ꮕ, ᏳᎾᎵ,ᏣᏙᎾ, in the Cherokee Bible. ᏃᏭ, ᏲᏁᎩᎭ ᏥᏩᎾᎵ,ᏣᏗᎲ so that everybody would understand what they read about. They did good, they did real good. ᎠᏯ’Ꮕ, ᏥᎧᎵ ᏥᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᎩᏄᎸᏅᎢ [ᎤᏰᏣᏍᎦ] ᎠᏬᏪᎶᏗ ᎠᎩᎪᎵᏰᏗ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ,
segments.translation: Yeah, you betcha. We went to their church in Westville to go visit them. They preached in all Cherokee, and also when they preached in the Cherokee Bible they would preach it in English, so everyone could understand what they read about. They did good. They did really good, and I am full Cherokee, and I can’t write or read it.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎦᎪ,--ᎦᎩ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏧᎶᏒ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ? ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᎠᏂ-Jehovah Witnesses ᎤᎾᎾ Westville ᏧᎶᏒ ᎠᏮᎨᏩ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ‘ᏙᎬ ᏴᏓ,? Cowboy ᏗᎧᎾ,Ꮧ ᏥᎨᏒ
segments.translation: Who was it that came through that was a Cherokee teacher over that way for the Jehovah’s Witness? He was from Westville, I forget, what would you say? He looked cowboy. Who?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Who--?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Was he tall?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, Hammer, that’s Jarred Hammer.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: I guess that was him.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, he looks like a cowboy ᏍᎩᎾᎾ
segments.translation: Yeah, he looks like a cowboy, that one.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: He’s pretty tall.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I don’t think it was him I seen.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: It wasn’t?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎩᎶ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎴ ᏣᏁᏙᎲ ᎡᏙᏙ
segments.translation: It was some older-looking man with them, when they were at Dad’s.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: John Chewey’ᏛᎡ He’s kind of a heavy set old man?
segments.translation: It was probably John Chewey. Kind of a heavy-set old man?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, that is Chewey, yeah.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎦᏥᏟᎶᏍᏔᏅ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ Ꮎ ᏧᏬᏞ … ᏱᎬᎪᏛᏓ ᎩᎳ’ᏭᏴ

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Do you have the picture?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: I forgot what his name was.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Yeah, Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᏧᎵ,ᏎᎩ,’Ꭱ “Japan’Ꭱ ᏗᎩᎶᏒ ᎠᏯ,” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏣᎳᎩ,
segments.translation: It was strange when she said, “I am from Japan in Cherokee.”

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: In Cherokee?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: She was talking.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yep.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I was just like this [expression]. She was talking good.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I was enjoying listening to what they were saying.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏧᎾᎴᏅᎲ Ꮎ Jarred Hammer ᏣᎩᎾᏢᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ’Ꮫ ᏣᎩᏲᎤᎸᏨ ᏥᏐᎯ about four months ᏣᏩᏂ,ᏏᏅ I couldn’t—I couldn’t move around. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᎷᏨ Jarred Hammer to hire me. And I didn’t even know the man. ᎩᎳ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ, ᏣᏩᏓᏙᎵᏍᏔᏅ “ᏱᏍᎩᏅᏮᎦ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎢᎦᏁᎳᏅ “ᏱᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏌ,’Ꭱ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎢᎦ ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ ᏗᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ He [God] put me back to work. … Ꭽ ᏍᏊ ᏯᎩ-ᏯᎩᏯᎴᎬ ᏗᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ Jarred Hammer ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏧᎷᏨ “Are you Bill Pettit?” ᏧᏛᏅ “Yes, sir,” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎠᏯ’Ꮫ ᏍᎩᎾ” – “ᎠᏯ,’Ꭱ ᏍᎩ,ᏍᏕᎸ,Ꮧ ᎠᏩᏚᎵ ᏓᎬ-ᎬᎾᏢᏗ ᎠᏩᏚᎵ” ᏧᏛᏅ And I had just got done praying about it! ᏍᎩ ᏱᎾᏛᎦ, ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: When they first started, Jarred Hammer hired me. That was when I hurt my back. I laid down for four months. I could not move around. He came, Jarred Hammer. I didn’t even know the man. I had just prayed a little bit ago and I said to our Lord, “If you heal me, I will work,” I told him. You know I really liked to work, and he put me back to work. I didn’t even look for work. Jarred Hammer came himself and said, “Are you Bill Pettit?” I said, “Yes, sir, I am him.” He said, “I want you to help me. I want to hire you,” he said. And I’d just got done praying about it. That’s what he can do, ain't it?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yep, He will take care of us, you betcha. Yeah, ᏍᎩ’Ꮓ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎦᏥᏍᏕᎵᎲ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᏓ, ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᏣᏂᏍᎦᏰᎰ ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᏥᏄᎾ,ᏛᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᏂ,ᎦᏥᏪᎮᎸ “ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏱᏣᏚᎵᎮᏍᏗ, ᎢᏥᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ” ᏥᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏗᏣᏓᏅ,ᏙᎩ ᏗᎦᎶᏍᎨᏍᏗ”
segments.translation: Yep, he will take care of us, you betcha, yeah. That’s when I started helping them speak Cherokee. They seemed to be afraid to speak, they said. That is when I told them, “If y'all want to speak like that, let it come from your heart.”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s true, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: You betcha! ᏧᎾ,ᎴᏅᎲ ᏍᎩ ᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁᎲ Boy, they just ran with it.
segments.translation: You betcha, they started doing that, and boy, they just ran with it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Were they afraid or were they embarrassed?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: You could say they were embarrassed.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎾᏂᏪᎮ ᎢᎦᏓ, “ᏄᏓᎴ ᏱᏅᏥᏫ” ᎠᎾ,Ꮧ … ᎠᏂᏍᎦᏰᎲ
segments.translation: That’s what some say. They think they will say something wrong. They are afraid.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏃᏭ, ᏥᎦᏥᏰ--Jarred ᏥᏥᏰᏲᏅ he—he recorded me. ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎠᏎ ᏄᏛᏁᎴ
segments.translation: Then I taught Jarred, and he recorded me. I guess that is what he did.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ, ᏥᏂᏪᎠ, ᏗᏣᏓᏅ,ᏙᎯ, ᏧᎶᎯᏍᏗ, ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: It's true what you are saying, it has to come from your heart.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yep, you betcha. Otherwise, it ain’t going to mean nothing.
segments.translation: Yep, you betcha. Otherwise, it ain’t going to mean nothing.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That is true.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ … ᎠᎾ--ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᎾᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎩ, ᏍᏊ ᏍᏊ Ꭹ-Ꭹ-‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ, ᎩᎶ ᏳᎾ,ᏚᎵᏍᎨᏍᏗ, ᎤᎾᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏙᏗ ᎤᎾᏓᏅ,Ꮫ ᏓᏳᎴᏅᏓ, ᏯᎾ,ᏛᏁᎠ, ᎩᎳ’Ꮽ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏯᎾ,ᏕᎶ,Ꮖ
segments.translation: That’s also for the Cherokee learners. If they want to learn, it has to come from the heart. If they do that, they will learn quickly.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: You betcha! You better believe it. … ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏥᏂ,ᎦᏥᏪᎮᎰ Ꮎ ᎠᏯ, ᎣᏤᎯ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏱᏣᏛᏁᎳ, ᎭᎵᎮᎵᎨᏍᏗ I mean, He gave us the right to. Y’know? ᏴᏫ ᏱᏚᏂᎿᎸ No! Give thanks
segments.translation: You betcha, you better believe it. You know what I say to the ones I live with? If you do something, be glad. I mean, He gave us the right to. They will be mad, not give thanks. You know.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, he allows us all the time.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: You betcha!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: That is to be thankful for.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᏂᎦᏪᎠ, ᏙᎲ? ᎤᎭᎨᏙ … ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏱᎦᏓᏙᎵᏍᏔᎾ, ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏴᏫ, they keep on, keep on. Same thing. – Huh uh! ᏯᏓᏙᎵᏍᏔᎾ hold onto it! And it will come true.
segments.translation: Yeah, that is what it says in the Bible, ain't it? You know, if we pray for something, people you know, they keep on, keep on the same thing. No, when you pray, hold onto it and it will come true. It’s already in heaven, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Don’t worry about it.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Just throw it out of your head. It’s already in heaven, yeah. Yeah, ᏍᎩ ᏄᎾ,ᏛᏃ ᏴᏫ, ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏆᎾ,ᎪᏍᎪ why. Not enough faith? I guess.
segments.translation: Throw it out of your head. It’s already in heaven. That is what people do. I am amazed at why. Not enough faith, I guess.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: I guess, ᎩᎶ ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏯᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗ ᏛᏛᎦᏂ ᎩᎳ, ᎠᏁᎵᏍᎬ ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: I guess praying all the time is the only way he is going to hear it, they think, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏃᏭ, ᎯᎢ ᎾᎬᏁᎸ … David from the book of Psalms. ᏭᏓᏙᎵᏍᏔᏁ … whatever he asked for, 21 days ᎤᎶᏎ He wasn’t getting his prayer answered. ᏃᏭ, he was just about ready to give up. He prayed twice, to the Good Man. ᏃᏭ, ᎤᎷᏤ Michael the Archangel ᎠᏥᎷᏤᎴ ᏕᏫ, -- “’Ꮩ’Ꭸ - Why hasn’t he answered anything?” ᎤᏓᏙᎮᎸ “I prayed two times!” – “He heard you the first time,” ᎠᎪᎮᎴ “Hold onto that.” ‘ᎡᎾ ᎤᏂᎪᏓ, ᎠᏂ-Satan ᏙᏣᏟᎮ ᎡᎶᎯ,” ᎤᏛᏁ Michael. ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ “ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏕᎵᏍᎩ, ᏫᏥᏯᎾ, ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏁ … ᎰᏩ ᏃᏭ, ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏚᎯ, ᏗᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ so he can answer you.” ᏍᎩᎾ ᎢᎦ ᎾᏂᎠ, ᎠᏂ-Satan ᎠᏁᎯ,’Ꭷ ᎡᎶᎯ, … for the angels to be battling.
segments.translation: This is what they did to David from the book of Psalms. He prayed whatever he asked for, but 21 days went by and he wasn’t getting his prayer answered. He was just about ready to give up. He prayed twice to the Good Man. Then Michael the archangel came to David, and he said, “Why has He not answered anything? I prayed two times,” he told him. He said he heard you the first time. Hold on to that. Michael said, “I have been fighting many demons on earth.” He said, “I had to go get my helper, so now I have made the way so he can answer you.” That is how many demons are in heaven – for the angels to be battling them.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That is true.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎾᏥᏪᎮᎳ,’Ꮓ “ᎭᏩ” ᎠᎪᎮᎴ “ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ ᎠᏪᏅᏍᏗ, … Ꮟ ᎮᎾ, Gabriel ᏙᏗᏟᎭ” ᎠᎪᎮᎴ ᎤᎾ’Ꮓ ᏭᎵ,ᏌᎳ,ᏓᏁ That’s pretty good, ᏙᎲ? In the book of Psalms ᎪᏪᎳ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ or, in the book of David. Ꮎ in the Old Testament ᎤᎾ ᏴᎪᎵᏯ, yeah.
segments.translation: Then he told him, “OK, so now I have to go back. Gabriel is still fighting.” Then he rose up again. That’s pretty good, ain't it? That is written in the book of Psalms, or in the book of David in the Old Testament. You can read it there, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: About how old were you when you started school?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Five.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Did you speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Or did you know how to speak English?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: I [laughs] didn’t.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Where did you go to school?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Greasy.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I know, but I have to ask you.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎭᏅ,ᏓᏗᎰ Ꮎ -- Well, you probably did, huh? ᏣᏅ,Ꮫ ᏲᏁᎦ, … ᎠᏯ, ᏃᎦᏅ,ᏛᎾ, ᏥᏬᏥᏝ,Ꭼ
segments.translation: Do you remember, well, you probably did speak English. Dang, we didn’t know anything.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎤᎾ Greasy! Winnie Mae Vann ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏓᏕ--Oleta and them ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏥᏙᎨᏲᎲᏍᎬ … ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏥᏬᎬ,ᏔᏅ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏃᏦᎵ,ᎬᎾ, Oh my goodness!
segments.translation: There at Greasy, Winnie Mae Vann was teaching. Oleta and them used to teach us in Cherokee. If we used English, we didn’t understand nothing.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh my goodness!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Who was the teacher?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Who?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏝᏍᎪ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᎨᎮ Ꮎ Asbill? Sue Asbill?
segments.translation: Was it that Asbill? Sue Asbill.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Or was it…

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Faynell.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Faynell [laughs], yeah!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎯᎸ Ꮎ ᏕᏗᎾ,ᏙᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏗᎬᏁ,Ꮧ ᏥᏕᎩᏘᏁᎬ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏧᏦᏛ [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] ᎤᎾ ᏦᎦᎦ,ᏌᏛ
segments.translation: She always took us to the dentist; she drove a little car. We were sticking out of there.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏥᏙᎦᏘᏁᏒ ᎣᏥ--ᎣᏥᎯᎸᏍᎩ, Ꮎ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, fillings ᏥᏂ,ᏓᏅᏁᎰ [ᏫᎦᏒᏂ,Ꭶ,] ᎩᎳ’Ꮽ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ, ᎤᏞ ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏙᎩᎴᏍᏔᏅ
segments.translation: What about that one time they took a few of us and one of them boys. You know, when they put in them fillings. One of them boys had candy. Right then, we had to take them all out. Y'all had them like that.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: *ᎾᎧ* Ꮒ,ᏕᏨᏅ ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ, ᏓᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᏚᏂᎴᏍᏔᏅ [ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] Ꮎ’ᏛᎲ ᏥᏓᎾ,ᏓᏁᎲ Ꮎ ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ
segments.translation: Y'all were eating candy so y'all got them out. But the doctors would give you candy?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yes!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: When we came out.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They gave us candy.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: That is why I don’t have teeth.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: We were in the same grade this one.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Is that right?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, the same.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He was mean! No, he wasn’t.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: You betcha!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Y'all were carrying on.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh, man.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮭ’ᎨᏲ ᎢᎩ--ᏰᎩᏍᎦᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎢᏗᏬᏂᎲ Ꮭ’Ꭸ ᏱᏣᏅ,ᏓᏓ?
segments.translation: They didn’t tell us not to be talking Cherokee as far as I know.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: They didn’t.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏯ,’Ᏺ Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᎢᎦᏗ’Ꮕ, ‘Ᏺ ᎨᏥᏍᎦᎬ ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ
segments.translation: I didn’t remember that. Some say they were getting told not to.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏕᎦᎸᏂᎲ ᏙᎲ? … Like, at Dwight Mission ᏥᎩ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᎨᎦᏂᎸᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏙᎲ? Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ, or whatever language. ᏗᎨᎦᎸᏂᎮ just to get it out of their system.
segments.translation: And they were getting punished, ain't it? Like at Dwight Mission, they did them that way there, ain't it? For talking Cherokee or whatever language just to get it out of their system.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏣᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏕᎦᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎬ ᎨᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏳᎾᏅ,Ꮫ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᏒ ᎠᏎᏅ, Ma--Mama Ꭳ-ᎣᎨᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ,--ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎣᎩᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᎡᎵᏭ-ᎡᎵᏭ ᎣᏏ ᏣᎳᎩ,--ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎾᎯᏳ Ꮳ-ᏣᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᎦᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎬ
segments.translation: When I first started school, they didn’t know I spoke Cherokee but taught us to speak English. I was speaking pretty good English when I started back then.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh, yeah!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎨᏍᏗ, ᏳᎾᏅ,Ꮫ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᏒ … ᎩᎵ’Ꮕ,--ᎩᎳ, ᏯᎩᎿᎸᏍᏔᎾ
segments.translation: But they did not know I spoke Cherokee. Unless they made me mad.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Then you were getting on to them.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Then he spoke Cherokee.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You can’t even cuss in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: No, you can't.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: You can quickly tell when someone gets mad.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh, yeah!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: They speak everything. Boy.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᏙᏳ, that’s Ꮭ ᏱᏕᎨᏥᏍᎩᎾᏓ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ, Ꮭ’Ꭷ? That’s good. That’s very good.
segments.translation: That’s crazy, ain't it, that you can't cuss in Cherokee, but that’s good. That is very good.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: But they can talk dirty, you know.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yes, for no reason.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎩᎶ ᏣᎩ,ᏛᏛᎲᏍᎬ “ᏣᎳᎩ,’ᎡᎦ ᏕᎯᏍᎩᎾᏗ?” – “Huh uh! Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏱᏗᏥᏍᎩᎾᏗᏍᎪ” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ
segments.translation: Someone was asking me if I cuss in Cherokee, I said I don’t even cuss at all, I told them.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: It’s ain’t worth it. What’s it doing?
segments.translation: It’s ain’t worth it. What’s it doing?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: What good does it do?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎠᏩᏓᎵᏏ ᎠᎩᎧᎭ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᏌᏭ ᏍᎩ’Ꮽ ᏧᏍᎩᎾᏗᏍᏗ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏲᏁᎩᎭ ᎤᎯᏐᏙ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏥᏯᏐᎮᎠ, It don’t make you big. It don’t do nothing for you.
segments.translation: One of my grandsons, that’s all he does, just cusses, but in English. It is boring. I am getting on to him all the time. It doesn’t make you big. It doesn’t do nothing for better.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Ꮎ’ᏛᏲ ᏯᏆ,ᏛᎦᎾ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏓᏂ-ᏓᏂ,ᏍᎩᎾᏗᏍᎬ Ꮎ “F-bomb” ᏣᎾ,ᏗᏍᎬ “’Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ,--Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏗᎬ,ᏙᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏥᏂᏪᎠ,!”
segments.translation: If I hear them cussing using what they call the f bomb, I say, “What is the use of you saying that?”

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yep, it ain't worth anything.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: It’s nothing.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: It’s nothing.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᏩᏛᏏᏒ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎧᏁᏍᏗ, ᏗᏪᏅᏒ ᏗᏢ, Ꮎ’Ꮕ, Ꮎ’Ꮫ Ꮔ--Ꮝ-ᏍᏗ ᏄᏓᎴ Ꮒ,ᎦᏪᏍᎬ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, … ᏳᎿᎸᏣ, ᎨᏍᏗ,-ᎨᏍᏗ ᏱᏓᏍᎩᎾᏗᏍᎨ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏱᎧᏁᎬ ᎩᎳ’ᏭᏴ ᏯᏕᎳᎰ
segments.translation: When I was growing up, I never heard that kind of words. Towards my house, my dad said it a little different, but when he got mad, he did not cuss. When he spoke in Cherokee, you could quickly tell.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: That was more than enough, ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: That was more than enough, ain't it?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: You betcha!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᏳ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᏗ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ, ᏍᏊ ᎾᏂᏪᏢᏍᎪ
segments.translation: I wonder about what you are saying. Women say that, too.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Ah, that’s not good.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ,’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᏗᎾ,ᏛᏍᎩ, … ᎡᏧᎳᎭ’Ꮽ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏱᎦᏪᏍᏗ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎪ
segments.translation: Girls or young girls. They say it like it’s just something you say all the time.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏙᎲ! Like it’s a normal thing. Well, anymore it is!
segments.translation: Ain't it, like it’s a normal thing.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎥᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏄᏍᏗᏓ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᎾᎩᏪᏌ, ᏗᏪᏅᏒ ᏯᏂᎷᎦ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏯᏂᏬᏂᎯ, “ᏞᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏱᏁᎨᏍᏗ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏗᏪᏅᏒ ᏗᏢ, … ᏙᏱ ᏗᏢ, ᏪᎾ”
segments.translation: That is the way it’s going nowadays. But if they come to my house, I will say, “Do not be talking like that in my house. Go outside.”

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, they need to respect it, ᏙᎲ? You betcha!
segments.translation: Yeah, they need to respect it, ain't it? You betcha.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: How many of your children were there?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Gaw. Ꮟ’ᎾᎲ ᏐᏁᎳ, ᏐᏁᎳ, ᎨᎵ ᏥᏃᏥᎥ
segments.translation: Gaw, wait a minute – nine, I think there were nine of us.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Are you the youngest?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, Watie…

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Waite.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Watie’Ᏺ he’s a year ahead of me.
segments.translation: Watie is a year ahead of me.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: But we were all in the same grade.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I thought they were twins growing up.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: A lot did.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: All this time, I just realized it the other day.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Well I say!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Watie’Ꭱ “ᏥᏍᏗᏠᏱ,’Ꮕ ᎨᎲ” ᏥᏲᏌ, ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, “Huh uh!” ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ, ᏧᏰᎸᏎ “ᏍᎩ ᏥᏂ,ᏍᎩᏂᏪᏎᎲ!” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ
segments.translation: I said to Watie one time, “Y'all were twins?” He said, “No, I thought it was funny.” I said y'all were telling me that.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏃᏭ, … ᎾᎾ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏥᏩᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᎰ Watie, Hobo-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, Rex-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, ᏧᏂᏅᎪᏨ out of their classroom, to come be with me. So that nobody’d mess with me. ᏂᎦᏓ’Ꮕ ᏃᏭ, that’s where we grew up together in the classroom. ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᎾ,ᏛᏁᎸ ᏦᎢ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, Ꮭ ᏳᎾ,ᏚᎵᎮ ᎩᎶ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎠᏩᏕᏙᏙᏗ
segments.translation: When I first started school, I remember it was Watie, and I think Hobo and Rex, got out of their classroom to be with me, so nobody would mess with me. That’s when we were there all together in the classroom. They did that, them three boys. They did not want anyone bothering me.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: And they put them in there.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎤᏅᏌ, ᎤᏂ,ᏘᏲᏢ Nellie Mays. ᎤᏂᏔᏲᏎᎸ ᎤᎾ ᏫᎨᏥᏴᏔᏅ
segments.translation: They asked themselves, they asked Nellie Mays.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ‘Ᏺ’Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎾᏛᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ms. Mays, ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: Nellie Mays would do that, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, she was a good lady Ms. Mays.
segments.translation: Yeah, she was a good lady Ms. Mays.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏯ, ᎦᏅᏓᏗᎰ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏣᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏕᎦᎶ,ᏆᏍᎬ Marie ᎤᏍᎪᏂᎸ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏩᏛᏍᏗ ᎠᎦᎵᏍᎪᎳ,ᏓᏁᎸ’Ꮕ,
segments.translation: I remember when I first started school, Marie cried to go with me, and she let her.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Well, I say.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏞᎦ, ᏧᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ ᎤᎾ ᏥᏯᎥ [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] ᎬᏂ’Ꮽ ᎤᏁᏘᏍᏔᏁ Marie ᏃᏭᎴ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᏫᎤᎷᏤ [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] ᏣᏠᏱᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ
segments.translation: For her to go to school for a little while in the room I was in. Marie got tired of it and never came back. She was crying all the time.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Well I say!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎥᎥ Ꮎ’Ꮫ Ꮎ Little Jack ᎭᏅᏓᏗᎰ Ꮎ?
segments.translation: Yes, do you remember Little Jack?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh, yes

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Gah-lee.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏥᏭᏁᎬᏒ ᎭᏅᏓᏗᎰ Ꮎ Greasy School –or uh, Greasy Store ᎠᏂ-Girdner’s-Ꭲ Ice Killer ᏧᎷᏨ he took the bus. He took our kids to school. Little Jack ᎤᏁᎬᏒ ᏥᏩᏝᎥ Ꮎ wheel.
segments.translation: What about the time he passed out, do you remember? At Greasy School, at Greasy Store, the Girdners, Ice Killer came and took the bus and took the kids to school. Little Jack was passed out laying on the steering wheel.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Did he already pick us up or what?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That morning.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, ᎾᎯᏳ ᏑᎾᎴ ᎾᎯᏳ Ꮎ after school ᏱᎩ, ᎭᏅ,ᏓᏗᎰ Ꮎ he’d get change out of his pocket? ᏳᏬᏝ, ᏥᎨᎲ not all the time.
segments.translation: Yeah, that morning. You remember back then, after school, he would get the change out of his pocket. He would be sitting there. Not all the time.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Just sometimes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, ᏳᏓᎭ’Ꮽ, ᏲᏥᎷᏣ, ᏥᎨᎲ to go get a piece of candy. ᎤᎾ ᏥᏬᎦᏣᎥ early in the morning. ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏛᏁᎸ Watie ᏥᏥᏃᏎᎴ “Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏳᏓᏅ,Ꮤ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏙᏳ’Ꮕ, he gaves us money. I guess he thought it was after school. ᏦᎩᎴᏒ ᎠᏕᎳ ᎤᏬᏰᏂ, ᏦᎩᎷᏨ ᎤᎾ to our classroom. ᏭᏁᎬᏒ … ᏍᎩ ᏥᏭᏂᏯᏅᎲ Greasy School Nellie Mays – Ice Killer ᏣᎦᏘᏃᏢ
segments.translation: Just sometimes, we would get out to get a piece of candy. We were sitting in there early in the morning when he did that. I was telling Watie, “He doesn’t feel good.” And he gave us money. I guess he thought it was after school when we got the money out of his hand. When we came back, he was laying on the steering wheel, passed out. They went and got Nellie Mayes at Greasy School. She brought Ice Killer.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᏄᏰᎵ,Ꮫ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ Ice ᏃᏭ, ᏓᏘᏂᏙᎲ
segments.translation: That was the reason Ice started driving.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yep, ᏍᎩᎾ’Ꭱ ᏧᏂᎴᏍᏒ out of the driver seat. ᏥᏩᏥᎧᏅ Bunch-Ꭲ Nellie Mays’Ꮕ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, Ice took us on into Greasy School. ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᏭᎴᏅᎲ Ice Killer ᏣᎯᎵᏙᎲ
segments.translation: Yep, they got him out of the driver seat and Nellie Mayes took him back to Bunch and Ice took us on into Greasy School. It was about then when Ice Killer started driving.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮦ ᏄᏰᎵ,Ꮫ Gaw! Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏣᏁᏦᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏚᎩᏛ, ᏥᏙᎦ,ᏘᏂᏙᎲ
segments.translation: I never did know the reason why, gaww. Also, when we used to play ball. He would be drinking a little bit when he took us.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh heck.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Uh huh, ᎣᏣᏁᏦᏍᎬ ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏥᏙᎦ,ᏘᏂᏙᎲ ᎣᏣᏁᏦᏂᏙᎲ ᎪᎩ,
segments.translation: Yeah, when we were playing ball. He would take us that far playing ball in the summer.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: My goodness.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: I know... ᎦᎾᏰᎩ, ᏃᎦᏛᏁ ᎣᏂ, ᏗᏢ ᏲᎦᏣᎠ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏥᎨᏳᏣ,
segments.translation: I know... we were in danger. We would all be in the back, us girls.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: My God.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: But he treated us right, you know.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Little Jack.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: We were in there.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: And he had been drinking.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: We were running around everywhere playing ball.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: My goodness.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᎬᏱ ᎮᎾ, ᏦᎦᎴᏅᎲ ᏂᎪᎯ,Ꮈ ᏦᎩᏠᏍᎬ Ꮎ trophy ᏦᎩᏁᎸ “hard luck.” ᏍᎩ ᏳᏲᏟ, ᏃᎬ-ᎪᎬᏁᎸ
segments.translation: When we first started, we were always getting beat. They gave us the hard luck trophy. They did us that poor.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Hard luck trophy.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Gaww.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏌᏚ ᏙᎦᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎪᎩᏁᎸ … I thought, “Huh…”
segments.translation: We were about 11. They gave us one like that. I thought huh…

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: That ain't right, ain't it?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎭᏗ! … ᎦᎪ ᏍᎩ ᎤᏓᏅ,ᏖᏝ, ᎨᎲ I never heard of such a thing.
segments.translation: No, I wonder who thought of it. I never heard of such a thing.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: It’s almost like they were making fun of you.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Ain't it?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎪᎦᏕᎰᎾ,ᏗᎲ ᏙᎲ? …cause… ᏙᏳ,’Ᏺ Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏲᎦᏓᏅ,Ꮦ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᎾ,ᏛᏁᎸ Ꮶ--y’know, ᏦᏥᎨᏳᏣ’Ꮽ, ᎨᎲ Next year’Ᏺ Ꮭ ᎩᎶ … ᎣᎩᏠᏍᎬ’Ꮓ
segments.translation: I really didn’t feel good when they did that. We were just girls but the next year, nobody was defeating us.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Did you still have the trophy?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: We got mad.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᎭᏅ,ᏓᏗᎰ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, DJ Mays ᏥᎨᎲ Little Jack’Ꮕ, ᎨᎵ ᏧᏂᎷᏨ they had boxes, ᏥᏓᏂᏰᎲ Ꮎ softball gloves ᏥᏚᏂᎸ ᎭᏅ,ᏓᏗᎰ?
segments.translation: Do you remember that one time DJ Mayes, and I think it was Little Jack, came, and they were carrying boxes? They had softball gloves in there, do you remember?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏝᎩ? Yeah, they had American gloves; red, white, and blue. ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ rough ᏦᎦᏤᎸᏅ
segments.translation: You don’t? Yeah, they had American gloves – red, white, and blue.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh, they gave those to us.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yep, ᏚᏂᏁᏒ Little Jack … DJ Mays-Ꮕ, they brought them back in a big ol’ box full of them, for all the kids at school.
segments.translation: Yep, DJ Mayes and Little Jack went and got them and brought them back in a big ol’ box full of them for all the kids at school.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Oh, yeah! ᎦᏅᏓᏗ’Ꮫ Ooh! ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ DJ Mays ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, Ms. Mays ᎤᏪᏥ, ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᏗᎨᏲᎲᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ, ᏙᎲ? … ᏍᎩ’Ᏺ ᏥᏥᏍᎦᏰᎲ ᏍᏊ
segments.translation: Oh yeah, I remember that. Wooooo, that DJ Mayes, that is Miss Mayes’ son, he was our teacher, ain't it? I was afraid of him.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Oh, ᏙᏳ,ᏍᎪ? ᎠᏴ,’Ᏺ that was my favorite.
segments.translation: Really? Not me, he was my favorite.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He was friendly.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Who was the one with the short leg?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Mr. Issacs

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Mr. Issacs

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I liked him, too.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, he was a good man ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: Yeah, he was a good man, that one.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎤᏓᏅ,Ꮨ,’Ꭱ Mr. Mays ᏥᎨᎲ but ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏯᏛᏁᎮ? Huh uh! ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, Crowely ᏣᎬᏂᎸ ᎤᎧᏔ Ꮎ eraser ᎬᏗ,
segments.translation: Mr. Mayes was friendly, but if he was doing something, no. One time he hit Crowley in the face with an eraser.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh, I remember.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏙᎯ, ᏱᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁᎮ ᏥᏙᏛᎾ,ᏝᏃᎮ ᎯᎢ’Ꮫ ᏥᏥᎦᏙᏍᏛ Mr. Mays *ᎯᎢ* ᏥᏄᏛᏁᎸ ᏥᏭᏗᏅ *ᎠᎭᏂ,’Ꮫ* ᏥᏩᎬᏂᎸ
segments.translation: They would not be still. They were talking. I was watching Mr. Mayes. He did this [expression?] then he threw it. He hit Crowley here.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh my God.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh, and you didn’t laugh.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: You didn’t.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏥᏓᏩᎧᎾᏅ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏭ ᎤᏚᎵᎲ […] “Miss Kimble,” --ᏂᎪᎯ,Ꮈ ᏣᏬᏎᎰ--“ᏣᏚᎵᏍᎪ, ᏣᏰᏣ,ᏍᏗ?” ᏣᏓ, “Huh uh,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎠᏩᏅ,Ꮤ,’Ꮫ ᏣᏚᎵ ᏫᏣᏰᏣ,Ꮟ!” ᏧᏛᏅ [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ]
segments.translation: He looked at me he wanted to… He said, “Miss Kimble, do you want to laugh?” I said, “No.” He said, “I know you want to. Go ahead and laugh.”

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᎭᏅ,ᏓᏗᎰ Ꮎ CCF ᏥᏕᎩᏁᎲ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏌᏭ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ well, I had a sponsor. … ᎭᏢ, ᏥᎨᎲ? Washington, the state of Washington ᏧᏂᎩᏛ Boy, ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏁᎳ, Nellie Mays ᏓᏳᏅᎪᏨ office-Ꭲ *clicking sound* ᏗᎠᎢᏐ Watie ᏕᏥᎦᏅᏅ “’Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ,?” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᎩ, …cause she was walking heavy… [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] “ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᎩ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎤᎾ ᏧᎷᏨ y’know, our room. Boy, ᏗᎦᏙᎬ “Can I help you Ms. Mays?” ᏧᏓᏙᎮᎸ Ꮎ her son, DJ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏄᏛᏅ ᏣᎩᎪᎲ I said, “I didn’t do nothing!” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ And I didn’t do nothing! ᏃᏭ “I need to see Billy,” ᏧᏛᏅ “in the office.” – “I didn’t do nothing, DJ!” I stood up, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏫᏥ-ᏫᏥᏂᏴᎲ “I didn’t do nothing!” ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, “Ms. Mays needs to see you,” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏥᏩᎩᏴᏢ ᏥᏩᎩᏴᏢ ᏍᏊ “Hey, I didn’t do anything!” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ “I didn’t do nothing wrong!” – “I need you to sit down,” ᏧᏛᏅ “I want you to tell me what this is all about,” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏥᏭᎴᏒ envelope ᏧᏍᏚᎢᏒ And I had never seen a check before. Check ᎤᎾ ᎦᎴ “Who’s sending you money?” ᏧᏛᏅ “Why are people sending you money here at school?” – “I don’t know! So it ain’t my fault!” ᏙᏳ’Ꮕ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᎨ some people was sponsoring me. From Washington, state. State of Washington. $500 check, ᏥᎦᎸ … But she didn’t tell me--Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ ᏳᏛᏅ ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏛ ᏕᎧᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏚᎾ,ᏙᎥ ᏴᏫ, an old man, an old lady, and their daughter. “ᎯᎾᎾ” ᏧᏛᏅ “This is what come with it, you tell me what is in this,” ᏭᎾ,ᏏᏁᏒ Ꮎ box ᏥᏚᏩᏌᏙᏴ “I don’t want it,” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ “I don’t know what’s in it. I don’t want it,” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎯᏍᏚᎢ!” ᏧᏛᏅ And it was a basketball, football, ᏗᎿᏬ ᏥᏕᏢ,Ꮫ
segments.translation: Do you remember those CCFs we used to get? I heard one time that I had a sponsor – where was it? the State of Washington, that it came from. Boy, I heard Nellie Mayes come out of her office. I looked at Watie. He said, “What?” It wasn’t good ‘cause she was walking heavy. I told him, “It’s not good.” She came there in our room. She was standing there. Her son DJ said, “Can I help you, Miss Mayes?” She seen me and pointed. I said, “I didn’t do nothing.” And I didn’t do nothing, so she said, “I need to see Billy in the office.” I told DJ I didn’t do nothing. I grabbed him here [gesture]. He said, “Miss Mayes needs to see you.” So I went in, and as soon as I went in, I said, “I didn’t do anything. I didn’t do nothing wrong.” She said, “I need you to sit down and tell me what this is all about.” She got an envelope out and opened it. And I had never seen a check before. There was a check in there. She said, “Who is sending you money? Why are people sending you money here at school?” I said, “I don’t know. It ain't my fault.” Some people were sponsoring me from Washington. Washington State. There was a 500 dollar check in there, but she didn’t tell me that. She laid it on this side [gesture]. She started to tell me the names of the people – an old man, an old lady, and their daughter. “This is what came with it,” she said. “You tell me what is in this.” Then she pulled out that box. She pushed it towards me. I said, “I don’t want it. I don’t know what is in it. I don’t want it,” I told her. She said, “Open it.” There was a football, a basketball, and clothes in there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ‘Ꮩ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏍᎩᏴ ᏳᏩᏂᏌᏗ sponsors ᏥᏕ--ᏣᏁᎲ I mean, y’know ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮵ-ᏥᏓᏂᎧᏁᎲ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, Ꮎ Ms. Mays-Ꭲ ᏥᎾᏛᏁᎲ
segments.translation: I wonder why. She is responsible for the sponsors. When there was, you know, Miss Mayes would give them to the children. Miss Mayes was doing that.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh, really?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Well, I’ll be darn.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Cause ᎦᏅᏓᏗᎰ ᏳᏓᏛᏛᎲᎦ, ᏂᎬ “CCF you’re going to get,” ᏣᏓ, “ᏙᏘᏁᏏ, ᏂᎯ ᏂᎯ’Ꮕ,” ᏣᏗᎮ
segments.translation: I remember she would go ask them everywhere and say you are going to be getting CCF.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ’ᏛᏲ Ꮎ regular CCF ᏥᎨᏒ ᎠᏮᎨᏫ,Ꮢ ᎯᎳᏴ-ᎯᎳᏴ--ᎯᎳᎦ, ᎣᎩᏅᏁᎲ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎨᏍᏗ, ᎣᏂ Ꮳ-ᏥᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎬ $34 $32
segments.translation: I remember when it was regular CCF. I forget when they were giving us those. But the last time I remember, it was $34 or $32.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꭷ ᎨᎮ … Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ sponsor ᎠᏕᎳ, Ꮸ-ᏨᎩᏅᏁᎲ ᎠᏩᏕᏘᏱᏍᎬ, ᏃᏭᎴ Ꮷ--ᏓᏂᏍᏓᏲᎯᎲᎢ, ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎠᏕᎳ, Ꮳ-ᏣᎩᏅᏁᎲ but ᎢᎦᏓ, $50 $100 Gaw lee!
segments.translation: It was about that much. And the sponsor would give me money for my birthday and Christmas. They would give me $10, and some would get $50, $100. Gah-lee.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, my goodness.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: And you were saying, I just get $10.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: I was in poor shape.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ Nellie Mays “What do you want to do with it?” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ “I don’t want it,” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Well, let’s go give it to your mother,” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, “What’re we going to do?” She pulled me out of school! ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏣᎩ,ᏘᏅᏒ ᏥᏩᏥᏃᏎᎸ DJ Mays what we was going to do. Ꮳ-ᏣᏥᏍᏕᎸᎲ Mom ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᏁᏟᏴᏅ check, and it was $500. I’ll never forget that. ᏁᎳᎩ’Ꮕ, ᏥᏩᎩ,ᏘᏃᏢ school-Ꭲ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꮎ hallway ᏥᏄᏍᏛ … ᏙᏆᎴᎳ, ᏥᎦᏢ ᎨᎵ “SST” ᏥᎪᏪᎸ, you pull that string? Uh huh. *ᎯᎢ’Ꮲ* ᏂᎬᏅᎯᏓ, … “Before school’s out,” ᏧᏛᏅ “Before kids come out, why don’t you go play with that?” ᏧᏛᏅ … ᏃᏭ ᏣᏪᏲᏅ ᏂᎬᏁ,Ꮧ ᏃᏭ ᏥᏬᎩᏂᏅᎪᏨ ᎠᎨ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏮᏁᎸ ᎠᏭ’Ᏼ ᏧᏂᎩᏒ … ᏃᏭ ᎠᏴ, ᏍᎩ ᏥᎾᏮᏁᎳ, ᏍᏓᏱ, ᏣᎩᎾ,ᏏᏁᏒ dang, it went all the way through the school, ᏥᏭᏗ,Ꮲ [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] That was a good time. I had some—I had some good times ᎤᎾᎾ.
segments.translation: Nellie Mayes said, “What do you want to do with it?” I said I don’t want it. She said, “Let's go give it to your mother.” And so what are we going to do? She pulled me out of school and took me home. She told DJ Mayes what we were going to do. She helped Mom cash that check, and it was $500. I will never forget that. And she took me back to the school. You know, where the hallway was, there was a car there. I think it had SST written on it. When you pulled that string, it was this [gestures] long. “Before school is out, before them kids come out, why don’t you go play with that,” she said. She showed me how to do it, we went out, she did that to it, and it went just a short distance. When I did it, I pulled it hard. Dang, it ran all the way through the school. That was a good time. Boy, I had some good times there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎮᎵ’Ꭳ’Ꭸ ᎠᏎ Ꮒ,ᏨᏁᎮ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᎦᏎᏗ, Ꮷ--ᎤᏍᎦᏎᏗ, ᏧᏤᎸᏅ?
segments.translation: Do you think she was just messing with you when she pretended to be mad?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Oh, yeah! [ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] ᎾᎾ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, Watie Daddy ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎪᎯᏥ,Ꮚ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᏣᏥᏃᏍᎩᏒ Ꮎ Daddy ᏥᎨᏒ ᏳᏢᎾ, he would put it his pants…ᎤᎾ ᎤᏈᏍᏙ ᎤᎾ ᏣᏢᏍᎬ ‘Ꮦ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꮩ ᎡᎵ Watie ᏍᎩ ᏄᏛᏁᎸ Crowley Proctor marbles, a bag of marbles, ᏣᏥᏲᏎᎸ that bag of marbles? For a $100!
segments.translation: Oh yeah. What about that one time when Watie stole $100 from Dad? He would put his pants on his pillow. He would put it there. I don’t know how Watie done it. He bought some marbles from Crowley Proctor. A bag of marbles for $100.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Watie stole from him.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, Nellie Mays ᏥᏛᏲᎩᏂᏯᏅᎲ “’Ꮩ ᎭᏛᎦ,?” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ Watie ᎩᎳ’ᏭᏴ … ᏥᏬᎩᏂᏴᏟᏢ Crowley ᏥᎦᏙᎬ “Yeah, Watie is the one that gave me that dollar,” ᏧᏓᏙᎮᎸ But it was $100. “Where’d you get this?” Watie ᏣᎪᎮᎸ “Dad gave it to me,” – “$100?” ᏣᎪᎮᎸ Ꮎ ᎣᏂ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ $100. “I need to take you boys home,” ᏧᏛᏅ Daddy ᏥᎨᎲ Stilwell Canning Factor ᏧᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏥᏬᎩᏂᎷᏨ ᏥᏩᎩᎪᎲ pickup ᏥᏗᎲ ᎤᏦᏙᏗ, ᎤᎾ’Ꮽ ᏣᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᎩᎾᏫ
segments.translation: Yeah, Nellie Mayes called us over there. Quickly I asked Watie what he did. We went in there, and Crowley was standing there. He said, “Yeah, Watie was the one that gave me that $1.00,” he told her. “But it was a $100,” she said. “Where did you get this, Watie?” He told her, “Dad gave it to me.” She said, “$100?” That’s when I heard $100. She said, “I need to take you boys home.” Daddy was working at the Stilwell canning factory. When we got back, I seen the truck he drove sitting there. I started trembling.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: She probably called him, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, Watie ᏙᏓᎦᏗᏒᏂᎸ ᎠᏴ,’Ᏺ “*ᎯᎢ* ᏗᏢ, ᏫᎶᎯ!” ᏧᏛᏅ Daddy. Cause he knew I didn’t do nothing wrong! “*ᎯᎢ* ᏗᏢ, ᏫᎶᎯ!” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏥᏩᏥᎸᏂᎸ Watie. Yeah, “Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏅᏁᎮᏍᏗ, Billy!” ᏣᎪᏎᎸ “Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎤᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ!” ᏣᎪ-- ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏥᎨᏥᎸᏂᎸ rough – Mama’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎦᏐᎮᎲ Daddy’Ꮕ Leon ᏅᏱ, ᏧᏗᏅ’Ꭾ ᎭᎴ ᏥᎾᏥᏍᎫᏴ Daddy ᏥᎨᎲ That high porch? ᎤᎾ ᏧᏩᏂᎸ ᎤᎾ corner post, ᏅᏱ ᏍᏓᏱ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ chip ᏥᎾᎬᏁᎸ that board. ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᏥᎸᏂᎸ ᏂᎦᏓ, Ꮎ hanger ᎬᏗ, or wire.
segments.translation: Yeah, he rolled Watie around. Daddy told me to go that way. Because he knew I didn’t do anything wrong, he said, “go this way.” [gesture]. He whipped Watie. He said, “Don’t do that to Billy, I don’t want him to learn things like that.” One time, they got a bad whipping. Daddy got on to Mom. Leon threw a rock and almost hit Dad in the head on that high porch. The rock hit on that post. It hit hard so it chipped that board right there. He whipped them all with a hanger or wire.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Gaw.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎾᎾ Tex-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, ᏥᏭᏗᏍᎦᏢ ᏧᏂ,ᏗᎩ,ᏏᏓᏍᏗ ᏥᏓᏳᎦ,ᏌᏛ [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] ᏥᏙᎩᎧᏅᏅ … ᏃᏗᎩ,’Ꮫ ᎨᎵ ᏚᏙᎥ “ᏃᏗᎩ,’Ꮎ ᎭᏢ,?” ᏧᏛᏅ Daddy ᏥᎨᎲ “ᏙᏱ ᏗᏢ, ᎤᏁᏓᏍᏗ’Ꮲ ᏩᏯ” ᏣᎪᎮᎸ ᎤᎾ ᎠᎦ,ᏙᎵ, ᏥᏓᏳᎦ,ᏌᏛ ᎠᏭ ᏗᏐᎢ, ᏥᎨᏥᎸᏂᎲ … Dad ᏧᎷᏤ Daddy ᏥᎨᎲ porch ᏣᏬᏢ “ᎠᏴ’ᏛᎧ ᏃᏭ,” ᏣᏪᎵᎲ back porch-Ꭲ ᏣᏬᏢ *ᎯᎢ* ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏅ waiting for my whooping. ᏣᎩᏂᏴᎲ *ᎯᎢ ᏄᏍᏛ* “ᎯᏧᏣ,” ᏧᏛᏅ “ᎮᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᏄᎾᏍᏗ, ᎯᎢ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᏍᏕᏍᏗ, ᏂᎯ ᎭᏛᏒ” ᏣᏬᏎᎸ “ᎮᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏗᎬ,ᏙᏗ ᏱᎨᎮᏍᏗ,” ᏧᏛᏅ Daddy ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ, ᏥᏭᏴᏢ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, “ᏩᏍᏗ” ᏣᎪᎮᎸ Mom ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎯᎢ’Ꭱ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏓᎾ,ᏛᏒ” ᏣᎪᎮᎸ “Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎤᏴᏢ ᏗᏢ, --Wisconsin ᏗᏢ, ᏭᏕᏅ Daddy—“ᎤᎾ’Ꭱ ᏳᏁᏅᏌ, ᎠᏎᏅ, Ꮭ ᏯᏬᎯᏳ” ᏧᏛᏅ “ᎡᎵᏭ’Ᏺ ᏧᏬᏢ’Ᏺ ‘Ꮲ ᏛᏰᏏ, ᏌᏭ” ᏧᏛᏅ which was me! “ᎤᎾ’Ꭱ ᏳᏪᏅᏌ, ᏧᏍᏆᎸᏛ ᎤᎪᏗ, ᏗᎦᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ, ᎠᎾ,’Ᏼ” ᏧᏛᏅ By God, if I didn’t end up in Wisconsin! My day one when I got to Wisconsin, I went to work. ᎤᎾ That’s where I stayed hooked up. ᏳᏓᎭ ᎨᎵᎰ ᎡᎵ’Ꭸ Daddy ᏥᎨᎲ he made a way for me.
segments.translation: Tex went and hid. He was peeking out of the outhouse. He was looking for, I think he called him Nodigi, Daddy said, “Where is Nodigi?” They told him, “He is in the outhouse. His head was sticking out over there.” He was whipping them other ones. Daddy came while I was sitting on the porch. I thought, “It's me now.” I was sitting on the back porch. I was like this [gestures] waiting for my whipping. He grabbed me here [gesture] and he said, “Boy, don’t grow up being like they are. They are not going to be worth anything,” Daddy said. Then he went in. He said wasdi to Mom, “If these boys ever grow up,” - toward the north, Dad lived in Wisconsin for a while - “if they go there, they might, but I don’t think so,” he said. “But that one sitting there is probably going somewhere.” Which was me. He said, “If he goes there. There really is a lot of work there.” By God, if I didn’t end up in Wisconsin. Day one, when I got to Wisconsin, I went to work there. That’s where I stayed hooked up. Sometimes I think Daddy made a way for me.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes, he probably knew.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏥᎾᏥᏪᎮᎸ Mom ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎯᎢ ᎠᏂᏐᎢ, Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏗᎬ,ᏙᏗ, ᏱᏙᏛᎾ,ᏛᏏ,” ᏣᎪᎮᎸ
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what he told Mom. He said these others are going to grow and be worth nothing.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I can just see Tex looking.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏭᏟ ᏗᏢ, ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᏭᏗ,Ꮲ Daddy ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᏧᏬᏢ [ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] ᏥᏩᎦᏗᏒᏂᎸ … ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ ᏚᏬᎰᎾ,ᏔᏅ … Ah man! […] ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꮎ trash ᏥᎦᎧᎭ, by … Dorothy’s house now?
segments.translation: ??? was sitting there and got rolled around. He probably really dropped them. Ah man, you know the trash that was scattered.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏃᏭ “ᏃᏗᎩ,’Ꮎ ᎭᏢ,?” ᏧᏛᏅ “ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ” ᏧᏓᏙᎮᎸ Mama ᏧᏓᎧᏅ Ꮒ,ᏓᏳᏛᏓᏍᏛ [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] Dang! ᏥᏩᏥᎸᏂᎸ Man! Leon ᏳᏩᏂᏌᏗ, Man…rough ᏦᎩᎶᏒ
segments.translation: By Dorothy’s house. He said, “Where is Nodigi?” Mom said, “Over there.” She was looking that way. He was sticking out over there. Dang, he got a whipping! Oh my God, it was Leon’s fault. Man, we went through some rough times.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎾᏍᎪ, ᏥᏥ--ᏣᏂ--ᏥᎦᏁᎳ, ᏃᏭ, Dorothy ᎤᎾ’Ꭷ ᏥᏥᏁᎶ?
segments.translation: Y'all lived where Dorothy lives now, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yep!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎯᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᎤᎾ? Ꮭ’Ꮎ ᏞᎦ, ᎢᏣᏂᎩᏎ? Ꮭ’Ꭸ?
segments.translation: How long were y'all there? Didn’t y'all leave for a little while, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Oh yeah, Stilwell ᏦᎩᎷᏨ pretty much Stilwell ᏥᎦᏛᎯ, ᎠᏴ,
segments.translation: Yeah, we moved to Stilwell. I pretty much grew up in Stilwell.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎯᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏥᏥᏁᎸ ᎤᎾ Ꮟ ᏂᏣᏂᎩᏓ,?
segments.translation: How long did y'all live there before y'all left?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Well, ᏙᏳ, ᏯᏩᏓᏅ,ᏖᏝ, ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ Uncle Sam Beaver ᏥᏭᏂᎷᏨ …
segments.translation: If I really think about it, Uncle Sam Beaver moved there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: It was right after that.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I was in high school.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: It was then?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: When they moved there.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, Daddy ᏧᏲᎱᏒ we didn’t stay there too long. Stilwell ᏥᏃᎦᏛᏂ,ᏔᏅ
segments.translation: Yeah, when Daddy passed away, we didn’t stay there too long. We went to Stilwell.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Y'all moved to Stilwell quickly.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Stilwell. Ꮟ… I think we went back one time. ᏞᎩ, ᏥᏬᎩᎷᏨ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᎠᎪᎾ, ᏦᎩᎨᎯᏙᎸ
segments.translation: I think we went back one time for a little while, then hunger ran us off again.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᎪᎾ,’Ꭹ?! [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] … Dorothy-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, ᎯᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏃᏭ, ᎤᎾ ᏂᎦᏁᎶ?
segments.translation: Hunger! How long has Dorothy lived there?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Gaw lee! ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏚᎦᎸᎯ’Ꮕ, “ᏓᏩᏙᎥ” ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏭᏬᏪᎳᏅ ᎤᏁᎳ,ᏗᏍᏗ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᎯᎢ ᎠᏗ: “ᏳᏲᎱᏌ,” before his boys—her boys. ᏍᎩᎾ “ᎩᎳ’Ꮽ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏗᎨᏥᏁᎸ” ᎠᏗ Ꮎ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ you can’t do that. It’s gotta be stayed in the family, in the blood. ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, … ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᏴ, ᎠᏩᏤᎵ Ꮎ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ and three acres. ᎠᏎᏅ, Dorothy ᎤᎾ … ᏗᎦ,ᏘᏂᏙᎯ, ᏣᏯᎥ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏓᏩᏙᎥ ᎤᏃᏪᎳᏅ so she can live there for 35 years. … ᎠᏎᏅ, I ain’t living in Bunch, ‘Ᏺ ᎠᏴ,
segments.translation: Gah-lee, they messed up. They wrote her name down to be the only one that lives there. Now she is saying if she passes away before her boys, she is going to give one of them that house. You can't do that. It has to stay in the family, in the blood. Really, that house is mine, and three acres. But Dorothy put her name down when that lawyer was in there so she could live there for 35 years. But I'm not living in Bunch.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s true, it’s better if you just stay out that way.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎾᎯᏳ ᏨᎩᎷᏨ from Wisconsin 24 years ago ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏓᏲᎩᎦ,ᏐᏒ ᎤᎾ Maxwell Mt. y’know, towards the house. ᎭᎴ ᎤᎾ’Ꮽ, ᎠᏲᏟ, ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ ᏱᎾᏩᏠᏱᎸ ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎤᎯᏐᏗ, [emphasis added] ᏣᏮᏂᎵᏢ …and I stayed with Watie [for] about … 2 months… Sallisaw ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏂ,ᏔᏅ ᏧᎯᏐᏛ’Ꮽ …it was just … there was no love… y’know? …
segments.translation: When I first came back from Wisconsin 24 years ago, we were coming off of Maxwell Mountain right there [gesture]. I almost cried like a child. A sad feeling hit me, and I stayed with Watie for about two months. I moved to Sallisaw, and it was lonesome. It was just, there was no love, you know? Yep.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Bob’ᏛᏲ ᎪᎯᏗ, ᎾᏂᏁᎶ ᎠᎦᎸᎳ,Ꮧ, ᏗᏢ, ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: Bob has been living above there a long time.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Gaw lee. ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᏛᎪᏐᏂ, [ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] … ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎨᎰ ᎤᎾ’Ꮽ ᏙᎲ? Well, they weren’t—Sallisaw’Ꮫ ᏞᎦ, ᎤᎾᏁᎳ,Ꮫ ᎤᎾ
segments.translation: Gah-lee, he’s going to rot there. For him, it’s just there, ain't it? Well, I guess they lived in Sallisaw for a while.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Bob?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: But that was years ago. ᎤᎾ’Ꮓ ᏭᏂᎶᏎ Bunch-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ,
segments.translation: But that was years ago. But then they just went back towards Bunch.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Huh. [ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] ᎤᎾ ᏛᎪᏏ,’ᎡᏛ … ᎾᎯᏳ’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᏥᏕ--ᎪᎢ ᏥᏕᏣᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ ᎭᏢ ᏗᏢ,’Ꮓ ᏫᏣᎶᏎ? Cave Springs-Ꭲ Ꮭ’Ꭸ?
segments.translation: He's going to rot there. When you were going to school at Greasy, which way did you go, Cave Springs or where?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Stilwell.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You went to school at Stilwell?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yep.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏥᏥᏯᏛᏛᎲᏍᎬ Watie ᏍᏊ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, “’Ꮧ! Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾ ᏱᏩᏩᎴᏅᎮ” ᏧᏛᏅ ᎤᎾ Cave Springs “ᏩᎩ,ᏑᎵ,ᎪᏤ’Ꮽ” ᏣᏗᎲ ᏝᏍᎪ, ᏱᏫ,ᏚᏕᎶ,ᏆᎡ ᏞᎦ,?
segments.translation: I was asking Watie one time, too. He said he didn’t even start there at Cave Springs. He just quit. Didn’t he go to school for a little while?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, I thought he did.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I thought he went to school for about two years.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: At Cave Springs?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,’Ᏺ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎤᎾ ᏯᏪᏅᎲ I just came from Greasy [then] to Stilwell.
segments.translation: I never did go there. I just came to Greasy and then to Stilwell.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎠᏩᏅ,Ꮫ ᏂᎯ Stilwell ᏣᎶᏒ Ꮎ’Ꮕ, Watie “Huh uh! Ꮭ’Ꮫ … ᏑᏓᎵᏁᎢ, ᏥᏗᏯᎥ ᏣᎩ,ᏑᎵ,ᎪᏨ” ᏣᏬᎮᎮ
segments.translation: That is what I thought. I knew that you went to Stilwell and Watie, but he said no. He said, “We were in the sixth grade when I quit.”

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎤᎪᎳ, ᏥᎩ, [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] Huh uh! ᏧᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ’Ꮫ Watie, Cave Springs, yeah.
segments.translation: That’s why he ain't all there. No, Watie went to school at Cave Springs, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s what I thought.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ, Stilwell-Ꭲ ᏦᏤᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ, Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏅᏓᏗ ‘Ꮩ ᎬᏁᎸ ᏫᎦᎷᎬ …But I know he went to Cave Springs’Ᏺ… ᏂᎦᏓ, …all the boys did… ᎠᏴ, ᎠᏮᏌ,
segments.translation: But we lived in Stilwell. I don’t remember how he got there. But I know he went to Cave Springs. All the boys did except for me.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You didn’t want to go to Cave Springs.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: No, heck no, yep.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: So, when you finished, you did finish at Stilwell.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Huh uh. Mama ᏧᏲᎱᏒ …I would’ve…ᏁᎲᎾ, ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎡᏥ “self-pity” ᏣᏃᎮ …that’s what killed me. Yeah, and I was doing good in school. I was doing real good… ᎾᎾᎭ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ᎾᎯᏳ’Ꮫ Mom ᏣᏲᎱᏍᎬ ᎠᏓᏰᏍᎩ, ᏧᎯᎲ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, ᏧᎾ,ᏚᎵᎲ ‘adopt’ ᏂᎬᏮᏁ,Ꮧ Bill Louise-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, …and Mom [had] done signed the papers. ᎠᏴ, they just needed my signature. I never did it… ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏥᎬᎩᏁᎲ …right there by where we were at Chalk Bluff… ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ …and they were old… “ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏦᏍᏗᏲᎱᏒ” ᏧᏛᏅ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ, “Ꮭ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏱᏙᏍᏗᎧᎭ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏥᏙᎩᏂᎾ ᏂᎦᏓ, state ᏫᏛᎦᎶᏏ,” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎤᏰᎵ,Ꮧ, …we want to put you through college,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ ᎠᏎᏅ, Mom ᏥᏭᏲᎱᏒ ᎥᏍᎩᏃ ᎠᏮᏌ,’Ꮫ ᏕᎦᏓᏙᎵᎬ …and I just gave everything up… … ᎤᏔᎾ, ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏥᎬᎩᏁᎲ …once they died. And after Mom died…Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, …three months later… ᎾᏁᎲᎾ, ᏥᏄᎾᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ …so I would’ve had all [of] that… Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ ᏐᎢ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏭᎷᏨ Lyon Switch ᏦᏤᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎯᏯᏅᏓᏗ Tom Sanders Evette-Ꭲ’Ꮕ,?
segments.translation: No, 11th grade. Mom passed away. I would’ve, but Mom passed away. What they call self-pity, that’s what killed me. Yeah, I was doing good at school. I was doing really good. Those white people... it was then Mom was dying with cancer. Some elderly white people wanted to adopt me. Bill and Louis, and Mom done signed the papers. They just needed my signature. I never did it. They were giving me a house right there by where we were at Chalk Bluff. A house, and they were old. That old man said, “When we pass away, we don’t have any children. All that we have will go back to the state, and that is the reason we want to put you through college,” he told me. Then Mom passed away. I guess I was feeling sorry for myself. I just gave everything up. Yeah, they were giving me a big house, once they died. And after Mom died, three months later, those elders passed away. So, I would’ve had all that. And that one girl came when we lived at Lyons Switch – do you know Tommy Sanders and Evette?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏥᏭᎷᏨ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, Tommy Sanders ᎤᎾ city lake. ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏥᏃᏨᏁᎲ … ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, “ᎩᎶ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ, ᏣᏩ,ᏛᎰᎦ,” ᏧᏛᏅ “Blue pickup ᎤᏦᏓ, …he really needs to talk to you. It’s important.” ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, ᏥᎦᏘᏛ “He’ll be back,” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, ᏍᎩᎾ’Ꮫ ᎨᎲ Tommy Sanders. And I ain’t seen him. Cherokee Children Mission School…ᎣᏂ ᏥᏥᎪᎥ … “Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᎩᎶ Pettit ᎦᏁᎳ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏅ” ᏧᏛᏅ “ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏩᏚᎵᎲ ᎠᏓ, ri-rick ᎢᎦ ᏗᎩ,ᏍᏆᎵ,ᏎᏗ … ᏱᏣᏝᏅᏓᏕᎠ,” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, ᏥᏍᏓᏩᏛᏒ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꮎ ᎠᏂ-Waterdown …they had land right there, by Cherokee Children Mission School…ᎤᎾ ᏬᎩᏂᏴᏢ ᏕᏥᏍᏆᎵ,ᏎᎸ …I didn’t split it, he just wanted some overnighters… ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, rick ᎢᎦ ᏕᏥᏍᏆᎵ,ᏎᎸ ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, ᏙᎩᏃᏢ’Ꮽ, ᎤᎾ ᏔᎵᎭ ᏓᏰᎲ old-time lunch box. Bologna ᏧᏬᏢ ᏁᎳᎩ ᎧᏫ, chips-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, ᎣᎩᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᏅ …after I cut the wood for him… ᏙᏳ’Ꮕ, “Billy,” ᎤᏛᏅ--Huh uh! ᎠᎬᏱ “ᎦᎪ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏂᎯ?” ᎤᏛᏅ “Billy-Ꮕ!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎵᎲ” ᏧᏛᏅ “ᎤᎾ’Ꭱ ᎪᎢᏍᎪ, ᏓᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎠ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᏕᏣᎧᎭ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ,” ᎤᏛᏅ “Yeah,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎾᎥ ᎦᏁᎳ, …by Greasy school?
segments.translation: Tommy Sanders came one time, when we were working at City Lake. My wife said, “Some old man came to visit you in a blue pickup. He needs to talk to you. It’s important.” So I waited. He said he will be back. And it was him, Tommy Sanders, and I haven’t seen him... the last time I seen him was at the Cherokee Children Mission. He said, “They said there is someone living here that is a Pettit.” He said, “I was wanting you to cut me a rick of wood if you have time.” So, I went with him to the Waterdown's. They had land right there by the Cherokee Children Mission School. We went in there, and I cut it for him. I didn’t split because he just wanted some for overnight. So I cut him a rick. So we were just sitting there, and he was carrying two of those old-timey lunch boxes. He had made bologna, coffee, and chips. We ate after I cut the wood for him. He said, “Billy,”- no, first he said, “Which one are you?” I said, “Billy.” He said, “That’s what I thought.” He said, “Do your boy’s children that you have go to school at Greasy?” He lives near there, by Greasy School.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, he lives right by there.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎥᏍᎩᎾ “ᎠᏴ, Evette-Ꭲ’Ꮕ…” ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎠᏧᏣ, …I guess they adopted a son… “ᏙᏆᎴᎵ, ᎤᏢ” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏌᎷᏂᎨᏴ ᎾᎥ …way back, way back when… ᎥᏍᎩᎾ “ᎠᏴ, ᏂᎨᎲᎾ, ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ” ᎤᏛᏅ “Evette’Ꮫ Oregon ᏗᏢ, ᏫᏛᎦᎶᏏ,” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏛᎯᏴᏂ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏂᎯ ᎬᏁᏗ ᎠᏩᏚᎵ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎤᎾ ᏱᏓᎾ,ᏕᏠᎦ,” ᎤᏛᏅ I denied it. “Huh uh! ᏝᏗ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ Tom” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Ꮭ’Ꭸ ᎩᎶ ᏐᎢ ᏱᎨᎯᎥᏌ,?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏍᎩ’ᏭᏛ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎣᎩᎾ,ᏓᏙᎵᏍᏔᎾ, ᏂᎯ’Ꭱ ᏕᏣᏙᎥ, ᎤᎷᏨ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᏂᎯ ᎬᏁᏗ,” ᎠᏎᏅ, …I know I can’t control life and death… ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏪᎲ “Boy, ᏯᎩᎩᏎ” ᎠᏪᎵᎲ “ᏫᏛᏲᎱᏏ!” ᎠᏪᎵᎲ …that’s why I didn’t take it. Yeah. “I got ten acres” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᏁᎳᎩ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎬᏁᏗ ᎠᏩᏚᎵ” ᎤᏛᏅ I didn’t take it.
segments.translation: Him and Evet, one time they adopted a son. He said he died in car wreck near Sallisaw. Way back then, and he said, “When I pass away, Evet is going back to Oregon and leave all of that.” He said, “I want to give it all to you, and the children can just go to school there. I refused it. I said, “No, Tom, can’t you give it to someone else?” That’s it. When we prayed, your name came up to give it to you. I know I can’t control life and death, but that’s what he said. I thought, boy, I should take it. He is going to pass away. That’s why I didn’t take it. “Yeah, I got 10 acres and the house. I want to give you all of it,” he said. But I didn’t take it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He is still alive.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, Ꮟ ᎡᎯ, ᏯᏐᏰᎯ, ᏯᏗ,ᏢᏍᏛ …but that’s why I didn’t take it! Cause…ᏥᏍᎦᏰᎲ ᎤᏲᎱᎯᏍᏗ …like I said, I can’t control that. ᏥᏯᏙᎵᎬ’Ꮫ ᏴᏓ, I—I didn’t take it. … ᏍᎩ ᎦᏥᏃᏎᎰ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏔᏅ Diane ᏗᏍᏆᎸᏕ ᎤᎪᏗ, ᏴᏫ, ᏍᎩ ᎬᏩᏛᏁᎳ, ᎠᏴ, …trying to give me things. But, the way God’s law is, I didn’t deserve it… ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, …I don’t do nothing bad! It’s just, that I don’t serve Him like I should… … ᎤᏂᎪᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏴᏫ, ᏍᎩ ᏄᎾ,ᏛᏁᎳ, …trying to give me property… ᏩᎧ’Ꮽ, ᏂᎨᎰ … ᎦᏥᏃᏎᎰ ᎠᎾᎵ,ᏣᏙᎲᏍᎩ, “ᎮᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎿᏛᏁᎮᏍᏗ” ᎤᎾᏛᏁ ᎯᎢ’Ꭱ “Everything good, comes out of Heaven.” … “ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏥᎭᏛᏁᎠ,” ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏅ “ᎮᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᎩ, ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎯᎢ Ꮵ-Ꮵ-ᏥᏂᏣᏛᏁᎠ, ᎤᏚᎵ ᏂᎯ, ᎩᎶ ᏐᎢ, ᎯᏍᏕᎸ,Ꮧ” But I didn’t feel like I deserved His blessings. Yeah, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏰᎵ,Ꮧ, … I don’t take it.
segments.translation: Yeah, he is still alive. He will wave when he drives by. That’s why I didn’t take it, because I was afraid he would pass away. I can’t control that. I guess you could say I felt sorry for him. I didn’t take it, yeah. That’s what I tell them, Diane. A lot of people have done that for me, trying to give me things, but the way God’s law is, I didn’t deserve it. I didn’t do nothing bad. It’s just that I don’t serve him like I should. A lot of people have done that, tried to give me property as well as cows. I was telling that preacher. They said, “Don’t be doing that. Everything good comes out of heaven.” They said, “What you are doing is not good. This is what they are doing for you. He wants you to help someone else.” But I didn’t feel I deserved those blessings. Yeah, that’s the reason I don’t take.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎩᎶ ᎮᎾ, ᏱᏣᏁᎠ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏣᎩᏍᏗ, y’know?
segments.translation: But if someone is giving you something, take it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: You know.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ … ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᏩᏓᏅ,Ꮫ ᎨᎲ … ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᏣᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ,ᏙᏗ, ᏙᏔᏕᎳᎰᏏ, ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᏣᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ,ᏙᏗ, … ᏍᎩ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ, ᏁᎳᎩ’Ꮽ, ᎨᎮᏍᏗ y’know ᏍᎩᎾ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ … Ꮎ-Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏧᎾ,-ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ, ᏄᏂᏪᏒ “ᏞᏍᏗ’Ꭱ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᏯᎬᏩᏟᎮᏍᏗ” … ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏍᎩ’Ꮽ ᎢᎦ ᎠᎭ ᎩᏂ-ᎩᏂ-ᎩᏂᏛᎴᏍᏗᏍᎪ…
segments.translation: What I think is, or how I feel in my heart – if it’s helpful, you are going to know if it’s helpful. If it’s not, let it go. That is what I think, and also what I have heard from the elders. They said don’t put value in money, but that is what gets us through.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s it right there.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: But some are, how would you say it? Greedy.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit

segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎬ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏕᎸ,ᏙᏗ, ᏥᏩᏛᎯᏙᎰ ᎢᎪᎯᏗ ᎨᏒ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎠᎩ,ᏛᎴᎯᏍᏙᏗ, ᎨᏒ
segments.translation: As for me, I am glad I can find enough to help me to get through.

segments.translation: When someone believes that GOD will always do it. You are going to find your help. You are going to find help.

segments.translation: You betcha.
