segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, ᎠᏴ, ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᎾᏩᏛᏃ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ “ᎩᎶ ᏱᎦᏥᏍᏕᎸᎭ,” ᏣᏗ ᎤᎾ,ᏚᎵ ᎤᎾ,ᏈᏗ “Help the next person,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ Cause somebody’s gonna need help. Cause I had a lot of help in my lifetime. And I just want to give some back. ᎾᎾ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ Baldwin, Wisconsin. ᎤᎾ Ꮟ ᏥᏫᎨᎥ Wisconsin ᏙᏍᏓᏗ,ᏟᎲ Ꮎ ᏙᎩᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎯ, …he was a machine operator… ᏍᎩᎾ …he had his seat pulled back… ᎦᏟᎲ …it was about 4:30 in the morning. ᎠᏭ ᏫᎦᏅᏅ …Baldwin going towards St. Croix Falls. No houses ‘til maybe like, 10, 15 miles… ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ, …there’s houses everywhere… ᏙᏍᏓᏗ,ᏟᎲ …nothing but corn fields… ᏎᎷ ‘Ꮲ *ᎯᎢ* ᏂᎦᏛ … Boy, *ᎯᎢ* ᏗᏢ, …out of the east… ᏛᏗ,ᏟᎲ ᏙᏆᎴᎵ, ᎤᏍᏓᏱᏛ *ᎯᎢ* ᏗᏢ, …out of the west… ᏐᎢ, ᏛᏗ,ᏟᎲ ᎠᎩᎪᎲ …and we was a ways, yet… ᎠᎩᎪᎲ …signal light… ᎠᏴ, ᏦᏍᏓᎢᏒ ᏗᏢ, ᏛᏞᏏᏒ Boy, ᏛᏗ,ᏟᎲ …from of the east… ᏓᏳᏅᎪᏨ Boy, ᎤᏍᏓᏱᏛ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ, “Gaw darn it, Rick!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “They’re going to hit!” ᏃᏭ ᎤᎵ,ᏌᎳ,ᏓᏅ Rick “Who’s going to hit?” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏍᎩ’Ꮽ ᏄᏛᏁᎴ …and it was early in the morning. Dark. No yard lights. All we had was lights on the cars… ᎤᎵ,ᏏᎩ,’Ꮽ, ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ Ꮳ-ᏣᎬᏂᎴ …it just turned all their lights out… ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, ᏣᏥᎸ …that morning… … ᏙᏆᎴᎳ, ᎠᎩᏅᎢ, ᎤᎾ ᏅᏃᎱᎵ,Ꮧ, …emergency lights…ᏓᎩᏨᏍᏔᏅ ᏫᏙᎩᎾ,ᏓᎾᏫ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᏴ, *ᎯᎢ* ᏗᏢ, …the one that got hit?... ᎤᎾ ᏫᏥᏍᏕᎸᎮ Rick-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, *ᎯᎢ* ᏗᏢ, ᎤᎾ ᏳᏛᏁᎸ … Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, …you could see… Ꮎ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏄᏛᏅ ᎤᎾ ᎦᏅ,Ꭸ ᏃᏭ, …when they hit… *ᎯᎢ* ᏧᎵ,ᏍᏔᏁ …you could see her face… *ᎯᎢ* ᏱᎦ …on the windshield… ᎤᏍᏆᎶᎡ …and broke her back. ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏣᏥᎸ ᎠᏭ, Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏐᎢ, ᏥᏍᏕᎵᏍᎬ, *ᎯᎢ* ᏥᏄᏛᏅ …underneath the steering wheel… Ꮎ gear shift *ᎯᎢ* ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᏥᎦᎭᏛ …not—not through the skull, but just through the skin… *ᎯᎢ* ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᏅᎪᏨ ᏥᎨᎲ … Boy, ᎦᏁᎵ,ᏗᎲ ᎠᎩᎾ,ᏌᏁᏍᏗ ᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ …so I can help him… ᎭᏗ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ ᏃᏭ, ᎠᏩᏕᏲᎸ Ꮎ guardrail ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᎾ ᏩᏥᏌᏙᏰ …so I couldn’t get in over there… ᏏᏭ *ᎯᎢ* ᏗᏢ, ᏛᏩᏓᎾᏫ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᏩᎿᏪᏒ ᎾᏮᏁ,ᏔᏅ ᏦᎳᏂ, ᏓᏥᏲᏍᏔᏂᏒ …behind him… *ᎯᎢ* ᎾᏮᏁᎳ, “Try this door!” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎩᎶ … ᎦᏳᎳ, …I was going to try that door. I was going to take the window out… “ᎦᏳᎳ,’Ꮫ -- I done did!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎨᎵᎲ Rick ᎦᏙᎬ …and there was nobody else, but; me, Rick, and the people. ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, “I done did!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Try again!” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎤᎾ Ꮳ-ᎠᎬᏂᎸ ᎨᎲ …he was just, smashed… Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, moan ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎲ ᎤᏣᎥ “Tell him you’re going to be with him in a minute,” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, “Hold on, sir!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “I’m trying to get in—get to you! Just hold on!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏩᎩᏂᏴᎲ ᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ …and it was—and I’d done tried this door!... ᎢᏤ ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ, ᎤᏍᏚᎢᏒ Ꮎ door. And this is God’s honest truth, He knows what I seen! ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, “ᎭᏣᎥᎩ!” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎡᎵᏭ’Ꮺ ᏙᏳ, ᎤᏍᎦᏍᏗ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ” ᎤᏛᏅ “Just lean over the seat!” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ But he was talking in English! ᏙᏳ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ ᏂᎦᏪᎲ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᏍᏓᏩᏛᏍᏔᏁ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏫᏥᏂᏴᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᎩᎳ’ᏭᏛ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎩᎦᎨᎭ ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᏬᏰᏂ, ᏥᏃᏎᎸ …what I was gonna do… ᏃᏭ, “When you come, bring him back to the seat,” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎠᏍᎪᎵ, ᎯᏂᏴᎲᎢ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᏗᏍᏆᎸᏛ ᎤᏣᏛᎦ,” ᎤᏛᏅ’Ꮓ “ᎯᎵᏃᎮᏕᏍᏗ! ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᎡᏍᎦ, ᏛᎾᎢ, ᏗᏂᏍᏕᎵᏍᎩ,” ᎤᏛᏅ --Who called ‘em? There was nobody! ᏙᏳ’Ꮕ, Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ, ᏱᏚᏢᏍᏔᏁ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏍᎩ ᎾᏩᏛᏅ ᎠᏩᏣᎥ back-Ꭲ ᎩᎦᎨ *ᎯᎢ* ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎲ ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏗᏬᏰᏂ, ᏥᎵᏃᎮᏛ …I asked him his name. I asked—It’s what the guy told me to do!...ᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ’Ꮓ state patrol ᏥᏓᎩᎪᎲ ᏙᏓᏳᏔᏂ, ᏔᎵᎭ ᎤᏠᏱ Ꮎ--Well, before that... ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᏥᎪᎥ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏗᎧᎾ,Ꮧ …well, he didn’t have a face!... Ꮎ’Ꮕ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ …it was hitting everything of him!... But he did not have a face!... ᏥᎪᎥ “Okay,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ Red’Ꭱ ᏧᏄᏮ Red and black shirt. I even put it in a state patrol … Ꮎ …a witness? ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎠᏬᏪᎳᏅ …what I seen… ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, ᏥᏃᏎᎸ state patrol… “How long—How long ago did you do this training?” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “I ain’t never done nothing like this,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “How do you know what to do?” ᎤᏛᏅ “That guy out there!” ᏫᏥᏂᏴᎲ “That guy out there!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “He told me what to do.” – “What guy?” ᎤᏛᏅ “There was a guy!” ᏥᏃᏎᎸ …what he had on… ᎩᎳ spotlight ᏫᏚᏂᏨᏍᏔᏅ ᎡᏧᎳ, …and looked around… Ꮭ ᎩᎶ [emphasis added] ᏰᏙᎮ … ᏃᏭ Rick … “Rick!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Where’d that guy go?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “What guy, Billy?” ᎤᏛᏅ “That guy that was just here!” – “There ain’t nobody here, Billy,” ᎤᏛᏅ “Just us.” – My god, ᎮᏍᏗ’Ꭱ ᏳᎧᏖ … ᏍᎩ ᎾᎩᏪᎮᎳ, Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, …out there… ᏂᏥᏛᏁᎳ, Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, …I talk to him, I told him I wasn’t leaving him… ᏃᏭ ambulance ᏧᏠᎸ ᏥᏂᏴᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, “Don’t let him go,” ᎤᏛᏅ Ꮎ ᎯᎾ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, “Don’t let him go.” …I crawled over the seat… ᏥᏂᏴᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, …I crawled over his seat, with the ambulance people… ᏍᎩᏃ ᏄᏅᏁᎸ *ᎯᎢ* ᏄᏍᏛ … so, ᏃᏭ, eight months later’Ꮲ ᎠᏬᏠ Falls Creek. ᎩᎳ’Ꮽ, ᏍᏊ ᎠᎩᎷᏨ …from work… ᎤᏍᏗ, ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, ᏣᎩᎧᎭ ᏗᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᎤᏃᏴᎵ,Ꮢ “Don’t answer it!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ … ᎠᎩᏲᏏᎲ ᎮᎾ, ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, ᎩᎳ’ᏭᏛ ‘answer’ ᏄᏮᏁᎸ “Yeah, hold on. Dad, it’s for you!” – “Man!” ᎭᎴ ᏫᏓᎩ,ᏍᎩᎾᏛ ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, …I got to the phone… “Hello?” ᏩᏩᏛᏅ “Yeah, hello. Is this Billy Petite?” ᏓᏳᏛᏅ “Well, it’s Billy Pettit,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ … Ꮎ “ᎯᎢ’Ꭱ ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ …about eight months back,” ᎤᏛᏅ “I was in a car accident,” Gaw lee, ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏥᏄᏪᎲ …I was back in that place… ᎩᎳ’Ꮽ, ᏫᏥᎪᎥ Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᏃᏭ, ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, …there’s a smart—smartass talk… ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꮎ “You saved my life,” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏃᏭ, ᎭᎴ “Did I kill a—y’know—a poop-eating dog?” ᎭᎴ ᏫᏂ,ᏥᏪᎮᎸ …but I held my tongue… “Oh, did I?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “How did I do this?” – “I was in a bad car accident,” ᎤᏛᏅ “My neck was broke in three places. One bad move [and] I would’ve died,” ᎤᏛᏅ “underneath that steering wheel. … You saved my life,” ᏓᏳᏛᏅ ᏃᏭ, ᏫᏥᏃᏎᎸ …what all took place… “Well,” ᎤᏛᏅ “I want you to…” ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎸ …his address… “—you’re our family,” ᏓᏳᏛᏅ I didn’t even know the man! “ᎠᏬ--ᎠᏩᏚᎵ ᏣᎷᎯᏍᏗ” ᎤᏛᏅ “And bring your family! … Let’s--Let’s be as one,” ᏓᏳᏛᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ …three places… ᎤᏲᏨ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᎵ,ᎨᏂ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏄᏪᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, …outside… ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᎤᏅ,Ꮦ …how bad he was injured. Yeah, and today, he’s still alive and well. Yeah, ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏣᎩ,ᏍᏆᎾ,--Well, Ꮭ’Ꮫ ᏯᎩ,ᏍᏆᎾ,ᎪᏌ, ᎮᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏳᎧᏖ …I could not see his face. It was just black ᏥᎨᎲ …and I seen everything else. *ᎯᎢ* ᏱᎬᏅᎯᏓ, brown ᎤᏍᏘᎬ …I could see that! Cause I wasn’t park that far from it. ᏍᎩᎾ, Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏩᏛᎮ ᏃᏭ, ᏥᎩ, ᏱᎪᎵᏯ, my statement ᎠᏬᏪᎸ …everything I seen that morning…
segments.translation: Yeah, me too. I'm right there. If I help someone, like you said, they will want to pay. I will say, “Help the next person, because someone is going to need help.” Because I have had a lot of help in my lifetime and I just want to give some back, yep. There was an incident one time in Baldwin Wisconsin, when I was still living in Wisconsin. Me and a co-worker were driving, he was a machine operator. He had his seat pulled back. It was about 4:30 in the morning in Baldwin, going towards St. Croix Falls. No houses till like 12 or 15 miles, now there are houses everywhere. We were driving through nothing but cornfields. The corn was this high [gesture]. Out of the east came a car, and it sped up. Out of the west came another. I seen it. We were a way yet. I seen the signal light. It was going to turn where we were coming. Boy, it was coming from the east fast. He sped up his car. I said, “Gaw dernit, Rick! They are going to hit!” Rick heard me and said, “Who’s going to hit?” Soon as he did that, it was early in the morning, dark, no yard lights. All we had was lights on the cars. It just got dark. When they hit, it just turned all the lights out. A girl got killed that morning, so I parked the car on the side of the road and turned on the emergency lights. We ran over there. I went to help the one on this side, the one that got hit, and Rick went to help the one that done it. That girl, you could see that’s how she was laying down. When they hit, she went like this [gesture]. You could see her face that big on the windshield. She hit her head and broke her back. She was killed right there, and the other he was helping was like this [gesture] under the steering wheel. The gear shift was stuck right here. Not through the skull just through the skin it came out here [gesture]. I was trying to open the door so I could help them, but nothing. So I went around. It was pushed against the guard rail, and I could not get in over there. So, I ran back around this way and took my shirt off and wrapped it – I was going to break the window behind them. When I did this, someone said try this door. I had already tried that door. I was going to break the window out. I said, “I done did.” I thought Rick was standing there, and there was nobody else except me, Rick, and them people. So I said, “I done did.” He said, “Try again.” He had been hit right there [gesture]. He was just smashed. The man was in there, moaning. He said, “Tell him you are going to be with him in a minute.” I said, “Hold on, sir, I’m trying to get in to you. Just hold on,” I told him. I grabbed the door, and I done tried this door. The door opened like it was new. And this is God’s honest truth. He knows what I seen. He said, “Get in. He is badly hurt.” He told me to just lean over the seat, but he was talking in English. So I did what he said and followed it. When I grabbed that man, immediately all of my arm turned bloody. I told him what I was going to do. He said, “No, when you bring him back to the seat,” he said, “hold his head. He is really injured. Keep talking to him. Help is already coming.” Who called them? There was nobody. Cars didn’t even go by. So I stayed like that in the back. The blood was going like this here on my hands [gesture], talking to him. I did what the guy asked me to do. I did all of that. Then I seen state patrols. Two of them came. Before that, I seen what the man looked like. He didn’t have a face, and the car was hiding everything of him, but he did not have a face. I seen him. I told him OK. He was wearing red, a red and black shirt. I even put it in the state patrol statement as a witness. I wrote it all down, what I seen. So I told the state patrol. “How long ago did you do this training?” he said. I told him I ain't never done nothing like this. “How did you know what to do?” he said. I said, “That guy out there.” I grabbed him and said, “That guy out there told me what to do.” He said, “What guy?” I said, “There is a guy.” I told him what he had on. They both shined their spotlights and looked around. Nobody was anywhere around. So I said, “Rick, where did that guy go?” I said to him. He said, “What guy, Billy?” I said, “That guy that was just here.” He said, “There ain't no guy, Billy. It’s just us.” By God, he did not have a face. That is what that man told me. Out there, what I did for that man, I talked to him, I told him I wasn’t leaving him. The ambulance came. I was holding him all that time. He said, “Don’t let him go, this man, don’t let him go.” I crawled over the seat and held this man. I crawled over the seat with the ambulance people and they did that to him here. About eight months later, I was sitting at Fall Creek. I had just got back from work. My little girl – the phone rang, and I said, “Don’t answer it.” I was hungry. She quickly answered it. She said, “Hold on. Dad, it’s for you.” Man, I almost cussed. I got to the phone and said hello. They said, “Hello, is this Billy Pettit?” I said, “It’s Billy Pettit.” This is what happened: they said, “About eight months back, I was in a car accident.” Gah-lee, that’s what they said. I was back in that place. I quickly seen that man again. Y’know, there’s a smart—smartass talk… Y’know, he said, “You saved my life.” I almost said, “Did I kill a poop-eating dog?” I almost told him that, but I held my tongue. I said, “Oh, did I? How did I do this?” He said, “I was in a bad car accident. My neck was broke in three places. One bad move and I would have died underneath that steering wheel. You saved my life,” he said. Then I told him what all took place. He said, “Well, I want you to...” He told me his address. He said, “You are our family.” I didn’t even know the man. He said, “I want you to come and bring your family,” he said. “Let’s be as one.” That’s what happened – his neck was broke in three places. What that man said, he already knew how bad he was injured, and today he is still alive and well. Yeah, that’s what I am amazed with. Or I am not amazed. He didn’t have a face. I could not see his face. It was blank, but I seen everything else: his hair was brown, about this long [gesture]. I could see that because I wasn’t parked that far from it. They never found anyone. You can read my statement. I wrote everything I seen that morning.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He put someone there to help you, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah. Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᎪᎯᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ ᏣᎩ,ᏍᏗᎬ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮫ ᎠᏩᏓᏂᎳ, ᎨᎲ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᎰ Mom ᏥᎨᎲ blankets ᏱᏓᏢᎦ, ᎨᎲ ᎤᏗᏞᎩ …trying to sweat it out, I guess?... ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏥᏅᎬ Watie *ᎯᎢ* ᏗᏢ, ᎦᏅ,Ꭼ ᎠᏴ’Ꮕ, ᎦᏳ,Ꮅ’Ꮕ, Daddy ᏥᎨᎲ ᏁᎲᎾ, ᎠᏴ ᎠᏰᏟ, ᏥᏅᎬ Mama ᏥᎨᎲ ᏦᎦ-- *ᎯᎢ* ᏄᏍᏛ ᎠᎰᏛ, ᏥᏅᎬ ᎠᏩᏗᏝᎲᏍᎬ ᎩᎳ’Ꮺ ᏧᏨᏍᏥᏢ …a lot brighter than this. In our bedroom…ᏧᏨᏱ,ᏍᏔᏂᏢ ᎠᏴ ᏥᏥᏅᎬ …usually I’ll pull the covers up…’Ꮵ,ᎩᎵ, ᏕᏥᏍᎦᏰᎲ [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] ᎥᏍᎩᎾ, *ᎯᎢ* ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏅ ᏥᏥᏅᎬ ᏧᏨᏍᏔᏂᏢ …and I looked at the … the light … it wasn’t even on, it was so bright in there, the lightbulb looked black! It looked burnt!... ᏙᏳ’Ꮕ, *ᎯᎢ* ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ “ᎭᏢ, ᏓᎦᎶᏏ,?” …Y’know, I thought somebody was up in the living room… ᎠᏎᏅ, …our bedroom was all lit up!... *ᎯᎢ* ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ ᎠᏭ ᎤᏟᏍᏗ, ᎠᏩᏗᏛᎲ ᎠᎭᏂ,’Ꭱ ᏥᎦᏙᎬ ᎤᏁᎦ, …against that door,…*ᎯᎢ* ᏥᏂ,ᏚᏮᏅ ᏧᏬᏰᏂ, ᏥᎦᏙᎬ …and I know what I seen… ᏴᏫ, ᏱᎦᏥᏃᏎᎳ, …”you were probably next to death. “Near death experience,” ᎠᎾ,ᏗᎰ …no it wasn’t…ᎩᎶ ᏨᎩᏅᏮᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎬᏩᏓᏂᎶᏒ … ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, ᏕᏥᎦᏅᏅ ᎮᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏳᎧᏖ …but again, I seen everything! I didn’t see no nail-scarred hands… *ᎯᎢ* ᏍᎩ ᏥᏂ,ᏚᏮᏅ ᏙᏳ, ᏣᏩᏂ,ᏏᏅ’Ꮽ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, *ᎯᎢ* Ꮒ,ᏥᏴᏁᎲ Mom ᏥᎨᎲ “Mom!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ Ꮎ ᎠᏨᏍᏗ, ᏙᎯ, ᏧᏠᏒ ᏃᏭ Mom ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏛᏡᏅ *ᎯᎢ* ᏂᎬᏁᎲ ᏥᎦᏅᎦᎵᎲ ᎠᎰᎵ, “’Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ, ᎤᏍᏗ?” ᎤᏛᏅ --Okay, before that…ᎠᎩᏰᏨ …blankets…ᏓᏢᏍᎬ ᏥᏅᎬ ᏃᏭ ᏩᎩᏢᏁ’Ꮫ …or whatever I did… ᎠᎩᏰᏨ *ᎯᎢ* ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᏐᎾ,ᏍᏛ Mom …on my chest… ᎩᎶ ᎠᎦᎵᏃᎮᏕ …and I didn’t no nothing about Jesus… ᎩᎶ ᎠᎦᎵᏃᎮᏕ ᎤᎵ,ᏏᎬ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏄᏮᏅ ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, *ᎯᎢ* ᎾᏮᏁᎸ “Mom, ‘Ꮩ ᎭᏛᏁᎠ,?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ *ᎯᎢ* ᏄᏍᏛ …she didn’t talk to me… ᏃᏭ ᎤᏍᏆᏛ,’Ꮓ “ᏩᏙ!” ᎠᎪᎮᎴ …whoever it was… ᎠᎢ ᏥᎦᏖᏃᎲ “ᎦᎪ, ᎠᎾ,ᏝᏃᎮᎠ,?” …and I thought I was hallucinating… Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏃᏭ, … ᏑᎾᎴ’Ꮫ ᎠᏩᏗᏛᎲ “ᎤᏍᏗ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎮᏍᏗ ᏃᏭ, ᏱᏓᏣᏓᏂᎶᏏ,” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎬᏩᏓᏂᎶᏒ … Yeah, and I was like, what? Seven? ᏥᏃᏎᎸ Mom ᏥᎨᎲ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᎩᎪᎲ ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, “ᎯᏢᎾ, ᏗᎾ!” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, …I went back to sleep! ᎠᎩᏰᏨ ᏑᎾᎴ ᏥᏔᎩ ᎠᎾᏴᎵ,ᏍᎬ ᏙᏥᏰᎢ,ᏍᏓ Mom “Mom! Mom!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Mom!” ᎩᎳ’ᏭᏴ ᎤᏟᏍᏗ, ᏭᏛᏅ “’Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎤᏍᏗ?” ᎠᎩᏂᏴᎲ ᎩᎳ’Ꮽ, ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᎩ,ᏒᏂᎲ “Gaw!” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎡᏣᏅᏮᎦ,Ꮷ!” ᎾᎯᏳ ᎬᏩᏓᏂᎶᏒ … And that’s like, 50-something years ago. ᎤᏴᏟ ᏯᎩᏂᏱ ᎠᏎᏅ, fever? [claps hands] Never.
segments.translation: Yeah, and long time ago when I was little, I guess I was sick all the time. I remember Mom would put blankets on me when it was hot, trying to sweat it out, I guess. One time I was laying there, Watie was laying on this side. Dad had already passed. I was laying in the middle and Mom on this side. I was laying there with a fever. Someone shined a light in our bedroom. They shined a light. I was laying there, and usually I’ll pull the covers up, afraid of the tsigilis. I was like this, laying there. They shined the light. And I looked at the light. It wasn’t even on, the light, it was so bright in there, the light bulb looked black. It looked burnt. Then I did this [gesture] and thought, “Where is it coming from?” I thought someone was up in the living room. But our bedroom was all lit up. I did this: I got up. It was standing there white against that door. He had his hands like this [gesture], standing there, and I know what I seen. When I tell people, they say you were probably next to death. Near-death experience, they say. No, it wasn’t. I was healed quickly. That was the last time I was sick. So I looked at it. It did not have a face. Again, I seen everything. I didn’t see no nail-scarred hands. He had them like this [gesture]. So I just laid back down. I was doing Mom like this, saying, “Mom” and that light slowly went off. Mom sat up, doing this [gesture], cleaning the tobacco from her mouth. She said, “What, little one?” OK, before I woke up, she was putting blankets on where I was laying or whatever I did. When I woke up, Mom was pressing here on my chest. She was talking to someone, and I didn’t know nothing about JESUS. She was talking to someone in the dark. She had it like this. I said, “Mom?” I went like this to her [gesture] and said, “Mom, what are you doing?” But she didn’t talk to me. So when she was done, she told him thank you, whoever it was. I was looking around to see who she was talking to. I thought I was hallucinating. There was nobody. She said, “When you get up in the morning, little one, you are not going to get sick anymore.” That is the last time I have been sick. Yeah, and I was like seven. I told Mom what I seen. She said, “Go to sleep.” So I went back to sleep. I woke up early in the morning and the chickens were crowing. Then I woke up Mom. I said, “Mom, Mom.” She said, “What is it, little one?” She grabbed me and started touching me. She said, “Gaw! You got healed!” I haven’t been sick since and that’s like 50-something years ago. I get a cold, but a fever, never.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏣᏗ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏍᎩ ᏥᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏣᎩᏰᏨ ᏥᏥᎪᎥ ᎩᎶ ᎦᏙᎬ ᏥᏅᎬ ᎾᎥ Ꮭ’Ꮕ, ᏳᎧᏖ
segments.translation: What you are saying happened to me once. I woke up and seen someone standing next to where I was laying and didn’t have a face.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: See? There.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏧᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ, ᏥᏕᎧᏁᎲ *ᎯᎢ* ᏥᏂ,ᏚᏮᏅ … ᎤᏍᏗ [emphasis added] ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ’Ꮕ Button-fly? ᏥᏓᏃᏎᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᏚᏑᎸ … Ꮭ--Ꮭ ᏳᎧᏖ
segments.translation: But they were carrying flowers, and held them like this [gesture]. He was a little man. He was wearing those - what do they call them, button fly? He was wearing some like that. He didn’t have a face.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Wow!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He had a lot of flowers, carrying them like this [gesture].

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Well I say.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, … ᎡᎵ’Ꮫ ᏔᎵ, ᎢᎦ, ᏧᎶᏐᏅ ᏥᏓᎩᏟᏆᏗᏅᏒ
segments.translation: And then after two days went by, I had a wreck.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Really, you wrecked a car.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Mhm.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Wow!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾᎲ “ᏓᏣᏲᎱᏏᏒ,” ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎮ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꭺ-- ᏧᏬᏚᎯ, [emphasis added] ᎮᎾ, ᏧᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ, ᏥᏚᏂᏰᏒ *ᎯᎢ* ᏥᏂ,ᏚᏮᏅ ᏙᏓᎩᏟᏆᏗᏅᏒ’Ꮓ
segments.translation: He was probably telling me I was going to die. He was holding some pretty flowers. He had them like this [gesture]. Then I had a wreck.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Gaw!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ … ᏥᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, … ᎩᎶ’Ꮫ ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎬ, … ᏥᏓᏂᏍᏆᎾ,ᎪᏗᏍᎬ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎠᏮᏁ,Ꮧ, ᏥᎨᏒ ᎠᏎᏅ, Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᎦᎪ,--ᎦᎪ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏍᏗ ᏣᎩᎪᏂᏲᎬ Ꮳ-ᏣᎩᎷᏨ ᎤᎾ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, Ꮻ-ᏫᏙᏗᏂᏯᎥ’Ꮽ, … ᏃᏭᎴ ᏣᏩᏠᏒ ᏃᏭᎴ ᎠᎩᏴᏟᏓ, ᏥᎨᏒ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏐᎢ, ᏙᏆᎴᎳ, ᏧᏠᎴ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏧᏠᏒ ᎦᏥᏲᎵᎦ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᏒ … ᎣᏍᏓ,--ᏙᏆᎴᎳ, ᎣᏍᏓ, Ꮒ,ᏗᎬᏁᎯ, ᏥᎨᏒ … ᎢᏂ, ᏱᎦᏘ,’Ᏺ Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᎤᏓᏅ,Ꮨ [emphasis added] ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᏒ Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏙᎩᎾ,ᏠᏒ ᎤᎾ ᏍᏚᏗ ᏗᎬ,ᏙᏒ ᎾᎥ … Ꮎ ᏧᏛᏅ “Boy, I just hate coming to these things,” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏧᏁᏨ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏲᏁᎦ, … ᎠᏴ--ᎠᏴ, ᏥᏓᏂᎸᏨ “ᎥᎥ ᏙᏳ, -- Me too! I know, I hate coming to this,” – “Well I guess I’ll go in.” ᏥᏭᏴᏟᏢ Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏯᏪᎵᏒ … ᏃᏭᎴ … ᏚᏂᏍᏆᏛ ᎤᎾ … ᏔᎵᏁ--ᏔᎵᏁᎢ, ᎣᎦᏝᏅᏨ ᏨᏥᎵᏃᎮᏗᏍᎬ … Ꮎ ᏥᏃᏎᎲ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎣᎩᎾ,ᏠᏒ … ᎠᏮᎨᏍᎬ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏚᏙᎥ Ꮎ’Ꮕ ᎤᎾᎾ Tailholt ᎤᎾ … ᏥᎦᏁᎴ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Ꮎ … I just got through talking to that, Ꮎ…” --ᎠᏮᎨᏫ,ᏍᎬ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏚᏙᎥ ᏣᎩᎧᏁᎸ “Huh?!” …I said, “Yeah, I just got through talking to him. You remember that guy that used to fix my car?” – “ᎥᎥ” ᏧᏛᏅ “He’s been dead for two years,” ᏧᏛᏅ [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] “ᏙᎯᏳᎢ! He’s been gone for two years,” ᏧᏛᏅ
segments.translation: That’s what happened to me one time. Someone was talking about it. They were having my cousin's funeral. I can't remember who it was. But I was a little late when I got there. They were already in there. I got out and went in. Another car pulled up and a white man got out. I knew him, he was a mechanic, a tall white man. He was friendly. I met him by the door. He said, “I just hate coming to these things.” I answered him and said, “I know, me too. I hate coming to these, too, so I guess I'll go in.” So I went in. I didn’t think anything. So when it was over, I talked to him a second time. I was telling him about what we had been through. I forget what his name was, but he lived at Tailholt. I told him I just got through talking to him and I forget what his name is. He looked at me. I said, “Yeah, you remember that guy that used to fix my car,” I said. He said, “Yes, he’s been dead for two years.” I said, “No, really?” “He’s been gone for two years,” he said.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: And you talked to him.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He came back.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏯᏪᎵᏒ … ᏂᎪᎯ,Ꮈ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, … Ꮧ-ᏗᏮᏁ,Ꮧ, ᏯᏂᏍᏆᎾ,ᏗᏍᎬ, ᏃᏭ, ᎤᎾ ᏫᎦᎷᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏓᏅ,Ꮨ, [emphasis added] ᎮᎾ, ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏥᎨᏒ … ᎤᏠᏱ ᏥᏚᏄᏮ ᎤᏁᎦ, ᎬᏅᎯᏗ, ᏗᎪᏯᏛ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎬᎿᎨ slacks ᏥᏚᏑᎸ ᎣᏍᏓ’Ꮕ, ᎤᎵ,ᏔᏬᏓ, ᏥᎨᎰ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, …every time we had a funeral… ᏍᎩᎾ ᏄᏛᏅ ᏥᏄᏍᏙ’Ꮽ, ᎤᎷᏨ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ…
segments.translation: But I didn’t think anything. Because every time they buried one of my relatives, he came. He was a friendly white man. He wore the same clothes: a white, long-sleeve shirt, and his pants were black slacks, and his hair was combed good. But every time we had a funeral, that is how he was. He came just like he was, but...

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: And he was already dead.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: I guess so, I guess so.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Was he not wearing those when they buried him? You know.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: For real, ain't it?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, it’s a possibility.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They may have put them clothes on him.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, something amazing like that can happen.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: My goodness, ᎤᎾᏍᎪ, ᏗᏢ, ᏖᎬ ᏂᎯ? Tailholt?
segments.translation: My goodness, are you from that way, Tailholt?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Huh uh. Ꮎ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᎤᎾ ᏓᏳ-ᏓᏳᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᎤᎾ’Ꭱ ᏗᏢ, … ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ ᏓᏄᎪ
segments.translation: No, Dad grew up there. But as for me, Vian.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Toward Vian.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: More toward Pinhook Corner.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh yeah, that’s right.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: This Billy Holcomb.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Billy Holcomb, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You remember Billy Holcomb.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, Billy Holcomb. I know Billy.
segments.translation: I know Billy.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They are related.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Y'all are brothers, just be quiet.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I knew you were going to say that. Not really.

segments.translation: And those Terrapins, you know them?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: A year… ᎯᎳ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ? About 8 years ago, ᎪᏪᎵ, ᎤᎷᏨ Albuquerque, New Mexico ᏧᏂᎩᏛ, ᏍᎩᎾ John Terrapin Alllic Beaver-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, ‘ᏚᏚ ᏥᎨᎲ five acres ᎬᎩᏁᎸ ᎤᎾ just on the other side of Tailholt.
segments.translation: Years ago, or when was it eight years ago, a letter came from Albuquerque, New Mexico. It had John Terrapin and Aleach Beaver, my grandfather. They gave me five acres just on the other side of Tailholt.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Is that right?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Mhm. ᏍᎩᏍᎪ, Ꮎ …towards Tenkiller School? Backroad ᏱᏫ,ᎦᎶᏌ,?
segments.translation: Yeah, is that toward Tenkiller School? If you go the backroad.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: You live on that?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎥᎥ I mean, Ꮎ’Ꮫ [Mitch] ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᏂ,ᎦᏫ, ᏱᏣᏃᎯᏌ,
segments.translation: Yes, I mean. He can say it better. He can tell you.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Let’s see…

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꮎ Caney Bridge? ᎢᏤ ᏧᏂᏒᏝᏛ?
segments.translation: You know where they built that new Caney Bridge?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Not too far from there. ᎤᎾ five acres ᎬᎩᏁᎸ …when I was a baby… ᎪᏪᎵ, ᎤᎷᏨ …saying I got five acres… ᎤᎾ
segments.translation: Not too far from there. They gave me five acres when I was a baby. A letter came saying I got five acres there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Would you say it’s past Sugar Mountain?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: It is towards Barber.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, Barber ᏗᏢ, Yes, yes,… It wasn’t too far from Ꮎ Tenkiller School.
segments.translation: Yeah, it's towards Barber, yes, yes, it wasn’t too far from Tenkiller School.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎭᏍᎪ Ꮎ … ᎡᎵᎩ, … ᎡᎵᎩ, Beaver ᏥᎨᏒ ᎤᏩᏁᎳ,Ꮫ
segments.translation: It's not where Elig used to live, is it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, do you know Elig?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏥᏯᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍᎬ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏥᏧᏣ’Ꮽ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᏥᎪᎥ
segments.translation: I remember him. I was just a boy.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, right there where you are talking about.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, and also Russell came.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: And Russell Beaver.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Was talking about that five acres.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎥᏍᎩᎾᎾ? Really? Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ ᏧᏂᎦ,ᏛᏅ Cherokee Nation …cause I was wanting to move one of them little houses on it. … ᎥᏍᎩᎾ, “ᏂᎯ ᏨᏌ, ᏕᏣᏙᎥ ᎪᏪᎳ,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, “…through all of them papers.” Ꮎ’Ꮕ, Been…Bean…Joe Bean. From Cherokee Nation? ᎠᏭ ᏍᎩᎾ “ᏂᎯ’Ꮫ ᏨᏌ, ᏕᏣᏙᎥ ᎪᏪᎳ,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ
segments.translation: That? Really, Cherokee Nation checked on that because I was wanting to move one of them little houses on it. That guy said, “Your name is the only one written through all of them papers. Joe Bean from Cherokee Nation there, he told me your name is the only one that is written.”

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Gaw.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: “I know your mom had a bunch of siblings. And their kids…” ᏧᏛᏅ “Somebody might throw a fit. ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏱᏨᏁᎳ,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ
segments.translation: He said, “I know your mom had a bunch of siblings and their kids. Somebody might throw a fit if you do that.”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They will do that, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: What about Sam Beaver? Did you know him?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: I have heard his name.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Davis, you know Davis.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh, yeah.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: One time… ᎤᎷᏨ Sam Beaver, Uncle Sam. Lyon Switch Ꮟ ᎣᏤᎲ “ᎮᎵ’Ꭸ--ᎣᏏᏍ ᏱᏰᎸ Billy,” ᎤᏛᏅ “Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎠᎩᎧᎭ, ᏳᏁᎳᏓ, …on the land?” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎤᎾ ᎠᏩᏅ,Ꮫ ᎨᎲ Bunch-Ꭲ “Oh, yeah!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Ꮭ’Ꭱ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏯᏅ,Ꮧ … Yeah, heck yeah. ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎾᎾ Bob Leon’Ꮫ ᏗᏣᏠᎯ!” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎭᏗ ᎩᎶ ᏧᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏲᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ “ᏂᎯ’Ꭱ ᏨᏌ,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ …I didn’t know that land was there. I didn’t know nothing about it ‘til two or three years later… “Yeah!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎤᎾ ᎨᎵ Davis Bunch-Ꭲ ᎡᎬ ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ ᎡᎨ ‘ᏚᏓ’s old land…
segments.translation: One time, Sam Beaver came. Uncle Sam was still living in Lyons Switch. He said, “Billy, would you be OK with it, if my son lives on the land?” As far as I knew, it was at Bunch. I said, “Oh yeah, they are not using it for anything. Yeah, heck yeah, it’s good with me,” I told him. But I said, “Talk to Bob and Leon.” But Sam said it wasn’t anyone's business. He said, “It is just up to you.” I didn’t know that land was there. I didn’t know nothing about it till two or three years later. I told him yes. I thought Davis was going to Bunch. He was going there, Duda’s old land.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Does he live there? Or not?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎤᎾ ᏥᏪᎲ ᏞᎦ, Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎤᎾ ᎨᏓᎵ ᏥᏭᎲ …Man, I didn’t know nothing about it ‘til that paper came in. “ᎭᏗ ᎩᎶ ᏐᎢ, ᏧᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ ᏱᎩ,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ Sam “ᏂᎯ’Ꮽ, ᎮᎾ, ᏨᏌ,” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ
segments.translation: He was living there for a little while. He had a little building down in that valley. Man, I didn’t know nothing about it till that paper came in. Sam told me, “It is nobody else’s business, just you alone.”

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Gah-lee.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, ᎾᎾ ᎯᏲᎵᎦ,’Ꮫ Bob … My brother, Bob, and Tammy? Ꮎ ᎤᏔᎾ, ᎠᏧᏣ, …the oldest one, Ray?...
segments.translation: Yeah, you know my brother Bob and Tammy and the big boy, the oldest one, Ray?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏥᎵᏍᎪᎸ,ᏓᏁᎸ ᎤᎾ …cause he didn’t have nowhere to go.
segments.translation: I let him stay there because he didn’t have anywhere to go.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s why he was living over there.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah! Right there, yeah. Nellie Sue’Ꮕ ᏗᏂ,ᏓᏂᏱᏍᎩ, ᏚᏓᏁᎴ …and she didn’t have no business. ᎭᎴ ᏥᏄᏂᏍᏚᏅ …for just sitting on that property, on that land, yeah.
segments.translation: Yeah, right there, yeah. Nellie Sue called the police. She didn’t have no business. They almost put him in jail for sitting on that property, on that land, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎢᏳᏪ ᎨᎲ ᏥᏥ--ᏱᏥᎪᏩᏔ, ᎡᎳᏗ, ᎠᎢᏒ ᎤᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᏥᏗᎦᎢ--ᏗᏢ, ᏣᎢᏒ
segments.translation: I would see him at any time walking, coming from there.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎤᎾ’Ꭱ ᏞᎦ, ᏧᎾ,ᏕᏅ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏯ, ᎤᎾ,ᎵᎪᎯ, … ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᎩᎳ, ᏥᎦᏅᎪᏨ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏍᏚᏗ Ray, about two days ago. Thursday ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, him and that woman stayed there for a while. He just now got out of jail, Ray. Two days ago, it was Thursday.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Is that right?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, they locked him up in Stilwell for about a year.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Do you remember when Dad lost his truck?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah. Did they do it? Did they do something to them?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Damn!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They said we can’t do anything to them.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: That’s a bunch of crap. That’s grand theft auto!
segments.translation: That’s a bunch of crap. That’s grand theft auto.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎥᎥ … ᎠᏭ ᏥᏬᎩᏩᏛᎲ ᏣᏍᏆᎾᎸ Ꮎ … Ꮟ Speedy’s-Ꭲ ᏫᏂ,ᎦᎷᏨᎾ, … Ꮎ feed store?
segments.translation: Yes, we found it was parked over there, before you get to Speedy’s, the feed store.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh, okay!

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They had ran out of gas.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: My goodness.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎤᎾ ᏣᏍᏆᎾᎸ … ᏏᏅᏓ, ᎾᎥ ᎤᏂᎯᎵᏙᎸ ᏂᎬ ᎠᎾᏝᏱᏙᎲ ᎤᎾ,ᏦᏛ … ᏴᏫ’Ꮕ, ᏥᏛᏂ,ᏗᎲ “Diane, ᏣᏙᏓ,’Ꭱ ᎤᏦᏙᏓ, ᎣᏥᎪᏩᏔ,” – “ᎭᏛ’Ᏺ” ᏧᏛᏅ ᎡᏙᏓ, “’ᎸᏢ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏂᏫᏛᎮ” ᏂᎬ’Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏓᎾᏝᏱᏙᎲ
segments.translation: It was parked there. They had it for about a month driving it around everywhere. People would call and say, “Hey, Diane, we seen your dad’s truck.” Dad said it can’t be. They took it somewhere. All that time, they were running around everywhere.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Gaw.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎤᎾᏦᏛ … ᏃᏭᎴ ᎩᎶ ᏥᏛᎤᏛᏅ ᏓᎵᏆ, “ᎠᎭᏂ,’Ꭱ ᎠᎭ, ᏗᏪᏅᏒ ᏥᏥᏲᎯ, … Ꮎ ᏍᏓᏱ ᎤᏍᏆᏃᏴᎩ,” Ꮎ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ ᏳᏅᏂ,ᏕᏓ, ᎨᎲ Ꮎ
segments.translation: They were driving it around. Then someone called from Tahlequah. "It’s parked here at my house.” “What y'all are looking at?” “It’s making a loud sound.” They had took that thing off.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Catalytic converter?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Converter. Oh, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᎾᏁᎵ,Ꮧ’Ꮕ, … ᎬᎩᏂ,ᏗᏅᏁᏗ,--ᎬᎩᏂ,ᏗᏁᏗ ᏑᏓᎵ--ᏑᏓᎵᏥ,Ꮚ ᎤᎾ,ᏚᎵ … ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, ᏃᏭ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎠᎭ,” ᏥᏓᏳᏛᏅ … Ꮭ’Ꭱ ᎩᎶ ᏃᏭ Erb ᏥᏫ,ᏥᏃᏎᎸ “Oh, ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ Ꮎ my renters,” ᏧᏛᏅ
segments.translation: They said they are trying to sell it to me. They want $600 and so it’s here, they said. I told Erb. He said, “Those are my renters.”

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Gaw.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I told him to go over there. But he didn’t go.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: My goodness.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,’Ꮓ ᏣᏩ-ᏣᏩ-ᏣᏩᏂᎩᏒ ᎤᎾ “ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏓᎬᎩᎸᏂᎸᎯ,” ᎠᏪᎵᎲ Ꮭ’Ꮓ--Ꮭ ᏯᎮ’Ꮓ ᏩᎩᎶᏌ,
segments.translation: So I left. I thought, “They are going to beat me up.” It wasn’t there when I went by there.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: They drove it again?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Yeah, ᏂᎬ’Ꭱ ᎤᎾ,ᏦᏗᏕᎨ ᏣᏅ,Ꮨ ᎤᎾ’Ꮽ Casey’s-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ, Stilwell ᎠᎮ Ꮎ ᏥᏚᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎠᏍᏆᎾᎸ ᎾᎮᎾ, ᎠᏂᏔᎵ, ᎠᏂᎨᏯ, ᏦᎦᎵ ᏑᎾᎴ [emphasis added] ᎮᎾ, ᏚᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎴᎪ “ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏂᎬᏩ,ᏍᏗ, ᏣᏙᏓ, ᎤᏦᏙᏓ, ᎠᎭ” Ꮎ ᏧᏛᏅ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎮᎾ, wheels ᏥᏂ,ᏚᏮᏅ Daddy -- ᏍᎩ ᎠᏃᎵ,Ꭼ ᏴᏫ,
segments.translation: Yeah, they said they were driving it around everywhere and it was parked at Casey’s in Stilwell where they work. It was parked there. Two women that I am friends with go to work early in the morning. They said, “It looks like your dad’s truck parked there.” Daddy had different wheels on it, and people were recognizing it.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh, okay.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: And where y'all used to swim.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Flat Rock.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Yeah, ᎤᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᏩᏗ,ᏟᏒ ᏍᏊ ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, they said it was going that way, too.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ ᏙᎲ Jimmy, my brother Jimmy? ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᏧᏂᎩᎡᎸ …he had a pickup…ᏧᏂᏃᏍᎩᎡᎸ … ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᏙᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ Tammy ᏥᏩᎦᏓᏁᎸ “You better get your damn boys outta my truck!” ᏥᏩ--ᏥᏩᎪᎮᎸ
segments.translation: And also Jimmy, my brother, they took his pickup away and stole it. I was there when he called Tammy. He told her, “You better get your damn boys out of my truck.”

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ “I’m fixing to call the Cherokee Marshalls,” -- ᎠᏭ’Ꮲ …transmission…ᏧᏂ,ᏓᏲᏍᏔᏁᎸ ᏍᏊ ᏓᎵᏆ,
segments.translation: He said, “I’m fixing to call the Cherokee marshals.” They tore the transmission up somewhere here in Tahlequah.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Gah-lee.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, that’s grand theft auto, by God. Everybody needs to be punished for something like that. ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏄᏰᎵ,ᏛᎾ, ᎠᏎ ᏧᏓᏂᏲᏍᎬ, …They’re just going to do it again!
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s grand theft auto, by God. Everybody needs to be punished for something like that there. Ain't no reason they should let them go. They are just going to do it again.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ,’Ᏺ inside’Ᏺ ᎤᏂᏲᏍᏔᏃᏅ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎭᏅ,ᏓᏗ’Ꮕ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏧᎲ?
segments.translation: On the inside, they kind of had it tore up. Do you remember he had that?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, that new one.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It was pretty.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, they have done a lot for them, ain't it?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: By God, where is their gratitude? My God.
segments.translation: By God, where is their gratitude? My God.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: But that’s that.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Okay.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎦᏥᏅᏆᏘᎰ ᏴᏫ, ᏥᏄᎾᏍᏗ, ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏅᏖᏗ …they don’t think! You gotta think before you do anything.
segments.translation: I get mad at people for the way they think. They don’t think. You've got to think before you do anything.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏓᏗᎰ Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏗᎦᏓᎨᏳ ᏱᎩ, ᏃᏭ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, Ꮭ’Ꭷ?
segments.translation: That’s what we say. We don’t love one another anymore.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: That is what it says in the Bible.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Respect, what is respect in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Is it to be liked? To be likeable? I don’t know what you would say.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏴ, … ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎩᎷᎶᏤ
segments.translation: I don’t either. That is what we are short on nowadays.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Oh yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Nowadays.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Nobody has any respect for anybody.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: To love one another.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Ain't it, that’s what you would say.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏱᏅᎦᏫ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏍᎩ ᏂᎬᏃ ᎤᎭᎨᏙ ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: Yeah, you could just say that. But that’s what it says in the Bible, ain't it?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It’s going to be like that.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yep. ᎥᏳᎩᎭ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ, …look how it is.
segments.translation: It going to be a time of sickness. Look how it is.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey

segments.text: ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, grate ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏂᎬᏁᎰ yeah, ᎤᏔᎾ pot. ᎾᎾ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, Strawberry Festival ᏄᏅᏅ Running Wolf ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎠᎩᎧᎭ …he was in a ballteam… Ꮎ the coach, Mark Holloway… ᎯᏲᎵᎩᏍᎪ,?
segments.translation: One time they were having that strawberry festival. That boy, my son Running Wolf, was on a ball team. The coach was Mark Hollaway. Do you know him?

segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, ᏍᎩᎾ …that was my boss… ᎤᎷᏨ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, Strawberry Festival ᏄᏅᏅ …and all the parents, they have to do… Ꮎ …he wanted everybody to help. You think you can cook about 72lbs of beans?” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “pinto beans?” – “You bet!” – “All at once?” ᎤᏛᏅ “We’re having a fundraiser,” ᎤᏛᏅ “Strawberry Festival. We’re going to sell Indian Tacos,” ᎤᏛᏅ Ꮎ’Ꮕ Thomas Muskrat’s ᎤᏍᏓᏴᏂᏙᎸ -- well she’s gone now, I believe.
segments.translation: Yeah, that was my boss. He came when they were having that strawberry festival. All the parents had to. He wanted everybody to help for a fundraiser, money for the kids. So, he asked me. He couldn’t say Bill. He calls me Will. He came and he said, “Hey, Will, you think you can cook about 72 lbs of beans? Pinto beans?” I said, “You bet.” He said, all at once, “We are having a fundraiser at the strawberry festival. We are going to sell Indian tacos. And Thomas Muskrat’s wife...” - She is gone now, I believe.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, she passed away.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: “ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎤᎪᏙᏐᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ” – “Oh, ᏙᏳ,ᏍᎪ?” ᎤᏛᏅ “…to make frybread. She is already doing that,” ᎤᏛᏅ “If you can do 72lbs of pintos? That tripod thing… ᎤᎾ ᏕᏥᎵᏴᏍᏓᏁᎸ …and I like to make my beans … Ꮎ soup thick? ᏍᎩ ᎾᏮᏁᎸ … ᏙᏳ,’Ꮕ, ᎢᎤᎷᏨ …and I had cooked all the 72lbs… ᎤᏫᏛᎲ … ᎤᎷᏨ …later on, after their sale… Ꮎ pickup-Ꭲ ᎧᎵ Ꮎ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ ᎤᏭᏢᏛ … “Man, what do you got in there? What else do you want me to cook?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “That’s all the lettuce and tomatoes,” ᎤᏛᏅ “Nobody wanted Indian Tacos. They just wanted your beans and frybread,” ᎤᏛᏅ [ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] ᏥᏭᎴᏒᎢ …that pot… “Yeah, ᏧᎾ,ᏛᎯᏍᏗ,” ᏣᏗᎲ “salt, ᎠᏂ-ᎠᏂᎯᏙᎲ ᎤᎾ,ᏕᎬ …in that pot. And then the frybread…” – It looked like it was washed.
segments.translation: That is most of it. He said, “We asked her to make fry bread. She is already doing that. If you can do 72 lbs of pintos, that sure would be of help.” I told him to bring me the stuff to do it with, so he brought a big pot. He said, “They have to be done all at once, one time.” I said, “Yeah, when you come back, they will be ready.” He brought a butane bottle and that tripod thing you can cook on. I cooked them on there for him, and I like to make my bean soup thick. I made them like that. So he came back. I had cooked all the 72 lbs, so he took it. Later on, he came back after their sale. He had something in the back of his truck. It was covered up. I said, “What do you have back there? Do you want me to cook something else?” He said, “That’s all the lettuce and tomatoes nobody wanted. For Indian tacos, they just wanted your beans and fried bread.” He got that pot out. He said, “Those old men had salt thrown in that pot and fried bread.” It looked like it was washed.

segments.translation: Dang!

segments.text: Yeah, “ᏙᏳ,’Ꮫ ᏚᏂᎸᏉ,ᏛᏅ” ᏣᏗᎲ …them pinto beans. ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ,’Ꭱ …that soup, to make it thick.
segments.translation: Yeah, he said they really liked them pinto beans. I like to make that soup thick.

segments.translation: Me too.

segments.translation: But they don’t like me.

segments.translation: Anything.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎯᎾ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏂᎬᏁᎰ bacon-Ꭲ ᏥᎩ, ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, … ᎾᎮᎾ, … ‘ᏙᎬ ᏴᏓ,? ᎢᏌ, ᏓᏆᏲᎯᎰ bacon ᏃᏭᎴ …puts it in the oven… Boy! ᎤᏍᏆᎸᏛ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: This is what my wife does with bacon. What would you say? Flour, she sprinkles on the bacon and puts it in the oven. Boy, it is very good.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Really? Put it in the oven?
segments.translation: Really? Put it in the oven?

segments.text: ᎡᏧᎳ,--Ꭱ-Ꭱ--ᎤᏠᏱ’Ꮽ, ᏳᏍᏗ, Ꮎ saltmeat ᎾᏅᏁᎰ …but, you can do it like—ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ‘ᏙᎬ ᏴᏓ,? … …rolls it in flour… ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏃᏭᎴ …real flat…--
segments.translation: They make it the same as salt meat, but you can do it like – how would you say it? Roll it in flour and real flat – how would you say it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: They bread it.

segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꭷ ᏴᏓ, …and lay them side by side and put it in the oven… Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎯᎳ ᏳᏗᏞᎬ, ᎨᎲ ᏂᎬᏁᎲ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, … Man! ᎣᏍᏓ,! ᎣᏍᏓ,!
segments.translation: And lay them side by side and put them in the oven. I don’t know how hot she makes it, but man, it is good.

segments.translation: My goodness, I can just see it.

segments.text: Yeah, ᎤᏍᏆᎸᏛ ᎣᏍᏓ, …You can make it as crispy as you want to. ᎤᏍᏆᎸᏛ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, it is very good. You can make it crispy as you want. It is good.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: My goodness.

segments.text: Ꮎ ᏧᏬᏢᏅ ᏙᏓᏫᏕᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮟ’Ꭱ ᏥᎩᎠ, y’know? Ꮎ ᎠᏘᏴ ᎠᏍᏆᎾ,ᎪᏗᏍᎬ …and she puts it on my sandwhich… ᏑᎾᎴᎢ ᏗᏢ,

segments.translation: My goodness.

segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎥᎥ ᏙᏳ’ᏛᏲ Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ Ꮎ ᎤᎦᎹ, ᏴᎪᏢᎾ, ᏍᏊ … ᏍᏊ two or three days, four--… ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᎩᎳ,

segments.text: ‘Ꮩ ᎠᏃᏎᎰ? Bean? ᏍᎩᏍᎪ,--Ꮭ ᏙᏳ, ‘bean bread’ ᏱᎨᎰ …but…ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮿ-Ꮿ-ᏯᏅ,Ꮣ, ᎢᎦᏓ, bean bread.

segments.translation: Bean patty.

segments.translation: Bean patty, that’s it.

segments.translation: That is what I make Daddy.

segments.text: Really? Ꮎ ᏍᏊ Ella ᏂᎪᎯ,Ꮈ ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ
segments.translation: Really, Ella makes them all the time.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.translation: And bean gravy. Oh my God.

segments.translation: Bean gravy? Not that.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Really?

segments.translation: What is that? How do you do it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾᎾ …It’s that juice from your beans… Ꮎ beans ᏚᎵ,ᏒᏅ ᏱᎩ, …you just make gravy out of it.
segments.translation: It is just that juice from them beans, when there are no beans. Just make gravy out of it.

segments.translation: She puts flour in it.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, just as you would gravy. ᎤᏖᏗ’ᏛᏲ
segments.translation: Yeah, just like you would gravy. It is good.

segments.translation: What about sour beans? You like them?

segments.translation: Yes.

segments.translation: I don’t.

segments.translation: No, that is what they make.

segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, Dad--Ꮎ ᏧᎾ,ᏦᏍᏛ-- “Huh uh! I can’t!” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ

segments.translation: You do this.

segments.text: Yeah, ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏗᎬᏁ,Ꮧ, Ꮎ patties ᏍᎩᎾ Ꭼ,ᏙᏗ,
segments.translation: Yes, that is how you use and do those patties.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: I love them.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: “Ꮭ’Ᏺ ᏃᏭ,” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎲ “Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏂ,ᎬᎦᏛᎦ,” – “ᏄᏓᎴ ᏗᏅ,ᏔᏅᎢ!” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ [ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ]
segments.translation: I am not – I told him I am not going to do that. I told him, “Let’s just use different ones.”

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᎦᏚ Ᏹ-Ᏹ-ᏱᎦᏥᏍᏗᎩ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, Ꮎ ᏚᏯ’Ꭹ Oooh, Ꮭ ᎡᎵ ᏱᏂ,ᎦᏛᎦ, … ᎤᏴᏍᏗ ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎰ
segments.translation: I can eat the bread, but the beans, I am not able to do it. It is too sour for me.

segments.translation: Really, oh, the sour.

segments.translation: The sourness.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Yeah, ᎢᎦᏓ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏚᏂᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, They’ll just let them sour!
segments.translation: Yeah, some like it like that. They will just let them get sour.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: They will eat it.

segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ …those refried beans. That’s how you make those refried beans.
segments.translation: And those refried beans, that’s how you make those refried beans.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎤᏗᏞᎩ, ᏱᏂ,--…if you make them--… ᎤᏗᏞᎩ, ᏱᏂ,ᏨᏁᎳ, …grease… ᏍᎩᎾ …three or four day-old beans from the fridge… ᏧᎾ,ᏦᏍᏗ, ᏍᏊ ᏱᎩ, …dump ‘em in there, black pepper’em. Dadgum…ᏧᏖᏙ …refried beans. Yeah, that’s what they are! In the can, even the commodity cans, them’s…sour…
segments.translation: Yeah, if it’s hot. You make that grease hot and three or four day old beans from the fridge, even if they are sour, dump them in there and black pepper them. Dad gum, they are good, refried beans. Yeah, that’s what they are, even them commodity cans. They are sour.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Dad gets those.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Yeah, you betcha.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: I can’t… ᎠᏎᏅ,’Ᏺ Daddy ᏕᏥᎩᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ Daddy ᏥᏓᎩᏁᎰᎢ
segments.translation: I can’t. I eat those, the ones Daddy gives me.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: They seem hard to me. Vegetarian beans, they say.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh, what kind are they? Are they just beans?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Just beans.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ, pinto beans. ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᏚᏮᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, just pinto beans. They are already cooked.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Did you say they are hard?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yes!

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: I think you can rerun them.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏱᏙᎬᏂᏍᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏙᏳ, ᏴᎬᏂᏍᏓ, ᏙᎲ? ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎲ Daddy “ᎯᎢ’Ꭱ Ꮭ ᏱᏗᎬᏂ,ᏍᎦ, ᏗᏍᏓᏱ!” [ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] “Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏱᏗᎬᏂ,Ꮢ ᏱᎩ,” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ “’ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏙᏓᏥᎩ,” ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᏗᏍᏓᏱ’Ꮕ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏱᏙᎬᏂ,ᏍᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: You can refry them, ain't it? I was telling Daddy, “These are not getting done. They are hard. They are not even cooked.” I thought I was really going to eat them, they were hard. But you can cook them again, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Oh, yeah, you betcha. Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᏦᏒ’Ꮽ, Ꮎ …Mama never had much food… ᏦᏣᏛᎯ, ᎤᏗᏞᎩ, ᏱᏃᏨᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ …then *so* much grease. Then just make…cornmeal-Ꭲ’Ꮽ, ᎠᎹ,’Ꮕ, …and then just dump the whole thing—whole thing in that hot grease… ᎤᏟ’Ꮕ, Mom ᏥᎨᎲ ᏚᏯ ᏱᏚᏝᎲ, …just make that corn—cornmeal—cornbread… ᎠᏲᏍᏔᏅ …just dump it on your bread, or on your beans.
segments.translation: You betcha. That was good, too. Mama never had much food, but we would make it real hot, then just so much grease. Just make cornmeal and water, and just dump the whole thing in that hot grease. Even more when Mom had beans, just make that cornmeal. Cornbread. Just break it up and dump it on your bread or on your beans.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Yeah, you betcha. Man! ᏦᏒ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ
segments.translation: Yeah, you betcha, that is good.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ Ꮎ ᏧᏪᏥ, ᏥᏓᎾ,ᏓᏁᎲ Ꮎ commod[ity] Ꮎ ᏥᏕᎦᏠ Ꮎ bags-Ꭲ
segments.translation: Those commodity eggs they give you that are in there in them bags.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Them bags, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Watie ᏣᏪᏲᏅᎢ …Ꭲ--ᏗᎬᏂᏍᏙᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᎬᏁ,Ꮧ … “’Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏣᏬᎮᎸ ᎠᎩ,ᏑᏴᏗ,? ᏦᎩᏃᏢᏅ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏖᏗ, Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏗᎩᎬ ᏱᎨᎮ Ꮎ
segments.translation: Watie taught me how to do those and cook them. What was it he told me to mix in there? We made it. I had never eaten them. They were good.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: The powdered eggs?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: The powdered eggs. Have you ever eaten them?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: I just thought, “Ah!” Yeah. ᏂᎪᎯ,Ꮈ -- Ꮭ’Ᏺ ᎠᏴ, ᏱᏙᏥᎦ, Ꮳ-ᏣᏪᏲᏅ Watie ᏱᎬᏁ,Ꮧ ᎤᎪᏗ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏦᎩᏂᏑᏴᏅ
segments.translation: I just thought, ah. Yeah, I am not going to eat them all the time, I thought. But Watie taught me how to make them. We mixed in a lot of things.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Gaw! ᎢᎦ ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ …with water gravy. Oh, my god.
segments.translation: I like that with water gravy. Oh my God.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎤᎪᏗ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ Ꮎ …grease… ᏦᎩᏂᏢ … ᏍᎩᎾᎾ’Ꮓ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏦᎩᏂᏢᏅᏅ … ᏥᏬᎩᎾ,ᏤᏮ ᎤᎾ … ᎤᏖᏗ,’ᎡᏲ ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ
segments.translation: We poured in a lot of grease. Then we put all of that in there and poured it out. It turned out good.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: You made kind of like an omelet.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᏗᎩᏓ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎤᎪᏗ, Ꮶ-ᏧᎵ,ᏑᏴ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎡᏚᏥ, ᏧᎷᏨ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᎩ,ᏝᎲ “Ooh! ᎤᏖᏗ,’ᏛᏲ ᎯᎢ!” ᏧᏛᏅ “Commodity cheese!”
segments.translation: A little bit like it, but there was a lot mixed in there. My uncle came when I had that on the table. He said, “This is good.” I said, “It is commodity.”

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏣᏗ omelet ᎠᏴ,’Ᏺ ᏍᎩ ᏂᎬᏁᎰ …them powdered eggs? I make like an omelet with it.
segments.translation: Like you are saying, omelet. I do that with them powdered eggs. I make, like, an omelet with it.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: You betcha! You betcha! Ꮎ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, shred ᏱᏂ,ᎬᏁᎳ, …cheese? Then I just put them on that. Heck yeah.
segments.translation: Or if you shred cheese and put them on that. Heck, yeah.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Ꮎ--Ꮎ powdered-powdered eggs Ꮭ … ᎤᏮᏌ, ᏱᎨᎮ Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎸᏉᏗ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, omelet ᏱᏗᎪᏢᏅ ᎣᏏ’Ᏺ ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ,
segments.translation: Just the powdered egg itself I don’t like it, but if it’s made into an omelet, it is good.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮎ’ᏛᏲ Ꮎ ᎤᎦᎾᏍᏗ ᏯᏬᏢᎾ, Ꮎ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏎᎷ ᎦᏚ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏕᎬᏗᎰ’Ᏺ
segments.translation: If I make a cake or cornbread, I use those.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: The powdered eggs?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: ᎥᎥ

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It is the same, yeah.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎤᏠᏱ ᏳᏍᏗ, if you used the regular eggs.
segments.translation: It is the same.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: It saves your eggs, ᏙᎲ? Daddy ᏳᏓᎭ ᎠᎩᏅᏁᎰ …one bag.
segments.translation: It saves your eggs, ain't it? Sometimes Dad gives me one bag.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Boy! That would be good ᏙᎲ? ᏓᏩᏚᎵ’Ꮓ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: That would be good, I want those now.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Or if I make those biscuits.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Gah-lee.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Boy, Dad can make biscuits, ain't it?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: You betcha, ᏙᎲ? ᎠᏑᏍᏗ’Ꮕ, My god.
segments.translation: You betcha, ain't it? And gravy, my God.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Well, ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏗᏗᏃᎮᏢᎦ, … ᏝᏍᎪ, ᏱᏍᏓᏚᎵᎮ ᏍᏗᏆᏗᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎪᎯ ᏥᏍᏗᏃᎮᎲ? … Oh! ᎭᏩ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎠᎩᏰᎸᎲ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᏓᏍᏛ … ᎭᏩ ᏃᏭ, ᏗᏗᏍᏆᏗᎢ Billy
segments.translation: Well, we really had a good conversation. Did y'all want to finish what y'all were talking about a while ago? I was enjoying listening. OK, we are finished now, Billy.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.translation: Alrighty, well I appreciate it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: What do you think is going to happen to our Cherokee language?

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: Well, ᏲᎱ’Ꭱ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎯᎢ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎦᏳᎾ,Ꮥ--ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ,’Ᏺ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏱᏛᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎢ, … ᎠᏴ ᎠᏬᎯᏳᎯ, ᎯᎢ ᏥᏓᏁᏲᎲᏍᎬ, ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ,’Ꭱ ᏥᏕᏓᏛᎯ, ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ ᏗᎦᏂᎩᏌ, ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ᏙᏧᎾ,ᏛᏅ ᏃᏭ, ᏱᏫᎩᎷᏣ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏴ,’Ᏺ ᎨᎵᎰ ᎯᎢ, ᏥᏓᏁᏲᎲᏍᎬ, ᎥᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᎦᎷᎶᎦ, ᏃᏭ, ᏥᏓᏁᏲᎲᏍᎬ, ᏱᏭᎵ,ᏍᏆᏓ, …that day… ᏳᎾᏂᎩᏌ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏲᏁᎩᎭ and…
segments.translation: It would be good if all these children learn to speak, but not all of them are going to learn. I believe these teachers now. You know how we grew up? When we come from school where the white people were, then when we get home, it’s all in Cherokee. I think what they are teaching now, that is what’s missing. When what they are teaching ends that day, when they go home, it is all in English.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s what ruins it.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎠᏲᏍᏗ Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏥᏄᏍᏛ Daver, Dave Pettie. ᎢᎦ Ꮎ …he got mixed up, English and in Cherokee. ‘Ꮩ ᏴᏓ, Ꮎ …he stuttered.
segments.translation: That’s what ruins it, yeah. That’s how Daver was, David Pettit. He got mixed up in English and Cherokee – what would you say? He stuttered.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Oh, yeah.

segments.speaker: billy-pettit
segments.text: ᎤᏍᏆᎸᏛ stutter ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ …that--that was why. He couldn’t comprehend it. English and in Cherokee. ᎤᏲᏢ’Ꮽ, ᏥᏂ,ᎦᏪᎲ [ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ]
segments.translation: He really stuttered, that was why. He couldn’t comprehend it English and Cherokee, it was sad what he was saying.
